scores.notes: Strongest repository under this lens by a wide margin, because the validity requirements are implemented AND tested rather than described. Chapter structure directly covers the sub-layer: 06_strategy_definition (universe rules, decision schedule, cost model, evaluation protocol), 07_defining_the_learning_task (triple-barrier/trend-scanning labels, IC, BH-FDR multiple-testing control, Deflated Sharpe), 16_strategy_simulation (vectorized vs event-driven parity, Deflated Sharpe + Rademacher Anti-Serum + White's Reality Check, 12_dsr_validation, 14_cost_sensitivity, 15-18 engine parity against LEAN/backtrader/zipline/vectorbt), 18_transaction_costs (spread estimation, market-impact calibration, VWAP/TWAP/Almgren-Chriss, breakeven costs), 25_live_trading (IB, Alpaca, QuantConnect, order state machine, pipeline verification). README states the 'evidence boundary' between exploration and confirmation and that purged walk-forward CV is used throughout. The tests/ directory is the decisive evidence: ~500 test modules named for exactly the failure modes in this lens — test_leakage_detectors.py, test_sp500_options_garch_pit.py, test_fold_free_temporal_features.py, test_latent_factors_no_leak.py, test_conformal_embargo_coverage.py, test_uncertainty_cscv.py, test_holdout_second_look_refusal.py, test_a_spent_holdout_window_refuses_at_registration.py, test_candidate_set_ranks_a_bankrupt_member_last.py / test_ranking_a_bankrupt_member.py (survivorship), test_cost_curve_scoping.py, test_nasdaq100_label_execution_basis.py, test_sp500_eoa_backtest_price_basis.py, test_us_equities_panel_*.py, test_ib_client_is_ib_async.py. US-equities coverage is first-class: case_studies/us_equities_panel (22 stages ending in 19_costs, 20_holdout_predictions, 21_holdout_backtest), us_firm_characteristics, sp500_options, sp500_equity_option_analytics, nasdaq100_microstructure. Reproducibility is operationalised: release v3.1.0-artifacts (2026-09-20) ships 860 training runs / 1,119 prediction sets / 11,099 backtests, each bundle recording its build commit in .release/SOURCE_COMMIT, and the release text flags that the sp500_equity_option_analytics bundle was built from a dirty worktree. CI (.github/workflows/test.yml) runs notebooks inside the published Docker images and, per its own header comment, runs the full matrix on every push to main after a documented coverage gap (issue #372: 59 of 122 shipped notebooks would not open) reached a reader. Docked on lifecycle_portability and quality_cost only for honest, documented cost: a full retrain is 73 GB of run logs and days of compute, four crypto model notebooks and the us_firm_characteristics deep notebooks are GPU-only, GBM on CUDA is not bitwise reproducible, and docs/what-this-is.md states plainly it 'is not a research platform and not a production trading system' with 'no turnkey path from a notebook to a running strategy'.

scores.notes: The most complete open-source factor/alpha + ML research platform for the sub-layer, and the strongest on measured, seed-averaged benchmark evidence. Backing paper arXiv:2009.11189. Upstream test coverage is broad and structural: tests/backtest/ (file strategy, high-frequency, soft-topk incl. cold start), dataset_tests, rolling_tests, storage_tests, ops, rl, plus test_all_pipeline.py and test_workflow.py; three CI workflows run the suite from source, from pip, and in a slow tier. scores.notes: Best-in-class for the 'automated factor/alpha research' half of the sub-layer, and the only candidate whose core claim is a peer-reviewed quant-research result. No survivorship control: the backtest is a user-supplied ticker x date grid, with no point-in-time universe construction.
Whether the LLM's pretraining corpus contaminates historical runs (the deepest lookahead risk for any LLM-on-history backtest) is not addressed anywhere in the README, CHANGELOG or tests.

scores.notes: The most rigorously de-leaked LLM trading-decision framework I could verify, but it answers a narrower question than this sub-layer asks. v0.5.0 (2026-09-18) is genuinely a point-in-time release: dated tools take the run date from graph state so 'an omitted or later date cannot reach a vendor' (#1331, #1319, #1118); SEC EDGAR fundamentals are served as filed, with unfiled periods withheld and restatements reading as first reported; insider filings and prediction-market odds are bounded by the run date; a feed that never observed a window reports unavailable rather than absent; the macro vintage pin is clamped to the vendor's own clock. The tests corroborate this rather than just asserting it — test_fundamentals_lookahead.py documents that both yfinance `Ticker.info` and Alpha Vantage `OVERVIEW` serve only present-day market cap / multiples / 52-week range and withholds them on one shared rule so switching vendors cannot reintroduce the leak, and it names the sibling leaks it belongs to (#1275 FRED, #1220 social, #1251 memory). Companion tests: test_news_lookahead, test_social_lookahead, test_memory_pointintime, test_tool_date_enforcement, test_undated_tools_as_of, test_yfinance_stale_ohlcv_guard, test_date_boundaries — ~70 test modules with CI. Backed by arXiv:2412.20138. Capability is capped at 2 because the output is a per-ticker Buy/Hold/Sell rating scored by realized alpha in `summarize`, not a strategy with a cost model, portfolio construction or an execution basis; and the README is explicit that 'backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure' and that the framework is 'a research scaffold for studying multi-agent analysis, not a strategy with a fixed, replicable return'. quality_cost is 1: every backtest cell is a full multi-agent LLM run, reasoning models ignore temperature so reproducibility requires deliberately downgrading to a non-reasoning model, and news/Reddit/StockTwits inputs still reflect 'now' even when the price window is pinned — so a historical sweep is both expensive and not re-runnable to the same answer.

scores.notes: Historically the most-cited open-source financial RL framework, but the README now demotes it in its own words, which is decisive under this lens. An IMPORTANT banner states FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading is 'the next-generation evolution' and 'Recommended for new users: Start with FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading if you are building modern or production-oriented trading systems'; this repository 'preserves the original end-to-end educational and research framework'. Its own comparison table concedes the gap precisely where this lens looks: Backtesting 'Custom hand-rolled evaluation loops' (FinRL) vs 'Professional bt library engine' (FinRL-X); Risk Management 'Gym environment constraints only' vs order/portfolio/strategy-level controls; Live Trading 'Basic Alpaca support' vs full multi-account integration. Citation weight is real (NeurIPS 2020 Deep RL Workshop, ICAIF 2021, ensemble-strategy ICAIF 2020 at 426 citations) and there is a test.yml CI workflow plus unit_tests/ for agents, downloaders, environments and preprocessors. But the strongest independent evidence cuts against it: AI4Finance's own NeurIPS 2022 FinRL-Meta paper writes that prior DRL market-simulator works 'are difficult to reproduce' and that FinRL 'focused on the reproducibility of backtesting performance by providing several market environments' — i.e. reproducibility of a backtest number, not validity of the research protocol. The quickstart trains on 2014-2025 and 'trades' 2026-01-01 to 2026-03-20 as a single split: no walk-forward, no purging, no embargo, no deflated Sharpe, no multiple-testing control. 312 open issues; last release v0.3.8 (2026-03-20).

unknowns: No US-equities result: the published experiments are PPO on BTC/USD only.

scores.notes: The only shortlisted repository that publishes a negative result about its own agent, which is strong evidence of honest evaluation even though the underlying capability is narrower than the sub-layer needs. Documentation covers the right protocol topics (05-advanced/01-overfitting Detection and prevention, 02-commission Key research findings, 03-walk-forward Proper evaluation, plus a 'Common Failures' track). Docked hard on maintenance: last commit 2026-02-09, last release v1.0.4 on 2026-02-06 — seven months stale as of 2026-09-21, and TESTING_REPORT.md is dated '2025-01-XX' with an unfilled day placeholder, tested only on Windows 10/11 + Python 3.13.1. scores.notes: The benchmark/environment layer of the FinRL ecosystem, and its stated purpose is the right one for this lens: 'To provide benchmarks and facilitate fair comparisons, we allow researchers to evaluate different strategies on the same dataset' and, explicitly, 'To reduce the simulation-reality gap: existing works use backtesting on historical data, while the actual performance may be quite different.' Peer-reviewed at NeurIPS 2022 Datasets & Benchmarks (openreview LkAFwrqdRY6), with follow-on work in Machine Learning (Springer, arXiv:2304.13174). Data layer includes Alpaca US Stocks/ETFs at 1-minute resolution from 2015, and it documents a train-test-trade pipeline that ends in paper or live deployment — the paper/live-parity intent is present. Most recent substantive work (2026-04-02, PR #360 'creating impact-aware market environments', env_mace) adds market impact, which is the correct direction. But maintenance is the problem: last commit 2026-04-02 (5.5 months), the latest tagged release is v0.3.6 from 2022-06-26 (over four years old) with 80 open issues, and the FinRL README positions FinRL-Meta as a legacy 'Market Environments' generation behind FinRL-X. The two PDFs checked into the repository root and the two-generations-old release make provenance clear but currency poor.

scores.notes: Correction to the shortlist metadata: has_tests is recorded as 'no' but tests are colocated with the code — hedge_fund/backtesting/test_backtest.py and test_fund.py, hedge_fund/event_study/test_event_study.py, hedge_fund/brokers/test_sim.py, hedge_fund/data/test_cached.py, test_client.py and test_client_contract.py, plus conftest.py. It is also better structured than the star count would suggest, with separate backtesting, event_study (engine/models/stats/plot), features, portfolio, risk, signals, strategies and pipeline packages, a mandate-file abstraction, and an event-study module that is a legitimate research primitive. That said it scores lowest on this lens among the actively maintained candidates, on its own testimony: the README opens 'This is a proof of concept... for educational purposes only and is not intended for real trading or investment' and 'Note: the system does not actually make any trades', and hedge_fund/brokers/ contains only protocol.py plus sim.py — there is no real broker adapter, so paper/live parity cannot be assessed at all. Costs are real and external: it requires a paid Financial Datasets API key for prices, fundamentals and earnings plus a model API key, and every rebalance runs LLM investor personas, so a multi-year backtest is expensive and non-deterministic with no reproducibility protocol documented. Maintenance is genuinely strong (v2.3.0 on 2026-09-18, ROADMAP.md and VISION.md describing a rebuild toward backtestable 'alpha models'), which is why the forward direction is promising even though today's research validity is unestablished.

scores.notes: A financial-LLM/sentiment model family, not a strategy research framework, so it is off-centre for this sub-layer even though the artefact itself is credible. The cost argument is the clearest measured result — LoRA adaptation under ~$300 against a BloombergGPT estimate of ~$2.67M in GPU hours — which is a genuine, checkable quantitative claim. It carries a tests/ directory (test_ashare_factor_benchmark.py, test_forecaster_market_sentiment.py, test_quantitative_sentiment.py, test_finetune_data_validation.py, test_market_symbols.py, test_transaction_data.py), but no CI runs them, and the most recent activity (Sep 2026) is a documentation-and-open-bugs sweep by an external contributor rather than maintainer feature work. Under this lens it is a component you would feed into a validated pipeline, never the pipeline.

scores.notes: The single most explicit disqualifying statement under this lens comes from the repository's own README: 'all scripts are historical data backtesting/forward testing... The assumption is that all trades are frictionless. No slippage, no surcharge, no illiquidity.' That is a stated, uncorrected violation of the cost requirement across every strategy in the repository, and the author further characterises the projects as 'quantamental analysis on some strange ideas I come up with to beat the market (or so I thought)'. Its genuine value is breadth of clearly-written, single-file reproducible implementations of published technical strategies — MACD, Heikin-Ashi, Dual Thrust, London Breakout, Parabolic SAR, Awesome Oscillator, Bollinger-band and RSI pattern recognition, pair trading, options straddle, VIX calculator, plus Monte Carlo and Oil/Ore Money projects — each with a `main` entry point, Apache-2.0, and near-zero adoption cost. But there is no validation protocol whatsoever: no walk-forward, no purging, no deflated Sharpe, no multiple-testing control, no US-equities point-in-time universe, and the strategies are largely FX/commodity rather than US equities. Useful as a reference implementation corpus, not as evidence about what works.

unknowns: No backtest, no benchmark table, no reported forecast accuracy and no trading result anywhere in the README or whitepaper listing.
No tests directory and no .github/workflows: nothing establishes that any component currently runs.
Whether the equity-report and forecasting agents apply any as-of-date discipline to fundamentals or news is unaddressed.
scores.notes: Lowest research validity in the shortlist for this sub-layer. It is an LLM agent platform for financial analysis, forecasting and equity-report generation (finrobot, finrobot_equity, tutorials_beginner/advanced, a FinNLP submodule, a web app and gcloud/deploy scripts), with a whitepaper at arXiv:2405.14767 and Apache-2.0 licensing plus an explicit disclaimer that the code 'should not be construed as financial counsel or recommendations for live trading'. But there is no evaluation layer at all: no tests/, no CI, no benchmark, no accuracy or P&L figure, and its bibliography cites other groups' agent surveys and FinAgent rather than its own measured results. Maintenance is effectively documentation-only — the last five commits are all 'Update README.md' (2026-08-23 to 2026-09-11), and the last non-README commit is 2026-05-10 ('gcloud deploy setup'). Under a research-validity lens there is nothing to verify.

sota_claims.claim: ML4T is the only shortlisted repository that enforces the strategy-validation protocol in executable tests rather than prose — its tests/ tree contains named regression tests for leakage detection, point-in-time GARCH features, purged/embargoed conformal coverage, CSCV, holdout second-look refusal and survivorship (ranking a bankrupt member last) — making it the strongest open-source reference for research validity in US-equities strategy research.

ML4T's v3.1.0-artifacts release is the most reproducible published strategy-research corpus in the shortlist: 860 training runs, 1,119 prediction sets and 11,099 backtests across nine case studies, with each bundle recording the exact source commit it was built from and the release text disclosing that one bundle was built from a dirty worktree.

Qlib is the most complete open-source factor/alpha research platform with a shipped point-in-time database (PR #343, 2022-03-10) and the only one publishing a 25+ model benchmark table with mean and standard deviation over 20 random seeds — but every published number is CSI300 / China A-shares, so its US-equities alpha quality remains unmeasured in-repo.

RD-Agent(Q) is the only automated factor-and-model research agent in the shortlist with a peer-reviewed quantitative result (NeurIPS 2025), reporting roughly 2x higher annualised return than benchmark factor libraries while using over 70% fewer factors at under $10 per run — a claim that is the authors' own and, as of 2026-09-21, has no public third-party replication and no US-market counterpart.

TradingAgents v0.5.0 is the most thoroughly de-leaked LLM multi-agent trading framework available, withholding present-day vendor company profiles on a single shared rule so a vendor switch cannot reintroduce the leak and serving SEC EDGAR fundamentals as filed — yet its own README states backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure, and it adds no transaction-cost or survivorship model.

limits: Evidence is documentary only. I read READMEs, CHANGELOGs, release notes, directory and test-file listings, CI workflow headers and a small number of test/doc file bodies via the GitHub API, plus Tavily/WebSearch results. I did not clone, install or execute any repository, so no capability, benchmark number or test-pass claim here is independently reproduced — the presence of a test file named for a safeguard is evidence that the safeguard is asserted and regression-guarded, not proof that it holds.

Test-suite evidence is weighted heavily in this lens, which systematically favours repositories that name their tests after failure modes (ML4T, TradingAgents, Vibe-Trading) over repositories that implement equivalent safeguards under generic test names. I could not read every test body, so some of that weighting rests on naming.

The shortlist was supplied to me; I did not run discovery, so absence from this list is not evidence of absence. Notable adjacent candidates I did not evaluate include FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading (which FinRL's own README designates as its successor), Trading-R1, mlfinlab/Hudson & Thames tooling, alphalens/pyfolio successors, and any Alpaca-org research repository.

Two mechanical-metadata items in the supplied shortlist did not survive primary-source checking: virattt/ai-hedge-fund is recorded as has_tests 'no' but carries colocated test modules in at least five packages, and je-suis-tm/quant-trading is recorded as pushed 2026-06-20 while its default branch (master) shows 2024-04-14 as HEAD. Other rows in that metadata were not re-verified field by field.

Performance and cost figures cited here (RD-Agent(Q) ~2x ARR under $10, FinGPT LoRA under $300 vs BloombergGPT ~$2.67M, TensorTrade's BTC/USD P&L table, qlib's benchmark IC/ICIR) are all self-reported by the projects themselves. I found no independent replication of any of them, and TensorTrade's is the only one framed as a negative result.

Point-in-time, survivorship and corporate-action correctness are properties of a data pipeline running against real vendor data, which cannot be judged from source listings. Where a repository is silent on one of these, I scored the item 0 and listed it under unknowns rather than inferring absence — but silence and absence are not distinguished by this method.

verdicts.claim: ML4T is the only shortlisted repo implementing CPCV/deflated Sharpe/walk-forward/embargo as named, CI-executed tests; 61/56/68 code hits vs 0 for each in qlib and RD-Agent.
verdicts.reason: Every number reproduced exactly via GitHub code search on 2026-09-22: deflated+sharpe 61/0/0, purged 56/0/0, walk_forward 68/0/0 (also combinatorial 13/0/0). The tests are genuinely CI-executed: .github/workflows/test.yml defines a `test-unit` job running `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/` (line 1014), described in-file as 'required and runs on every commit'; the Tests workflow shows conclusion=success on main at 2026-09-21T15:58:48Z. CAVEAT: the framing overstates. qlib does implement rolling walk-forward retraining under a different name (`RollingGen`, 8 code hits), so the 0-hit column reflects vocabulary, not total absence of walk-forward capability. The 'as named' qualifier is what saves the claim.

verdicts.reason: 690 confirmed exactly from the recursive git tree (689 under agent/tests plus tools/test_ci_env_var_gate.py), against 415 for ML4T, 72 for TradingAgents, 37 for qlib and 31 for RD-Agent. test.yml confirms the hash-lock job across ubuntu-24.04/macos-15/windows-2025 running `pip install --dry-run --require-hashes` on both lock files, and a test job on python-version ['3.11','3.14'] running `pytest ... --cov=agent --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml`. CI conclusion=success on main at 2026-09-21T18:25:45Z. Minor caveat: the pytest invocation passes --ignore for agent/tests/e2e_backtest and test_e2e_harness_v2.py, so 'executed' is 690 minus those paths (the e2e_backtest path currently holds 0 tree entries, so the deduction is ~1 file).

verdicts.claim: Most complete org-backed factor/alpha platform in the set; only one whose CI separately tests the published PyPI wheel and the source tree; README routes LLM factor generation to RD-Agent; no release since v0.9.7 on 2025-08-15.
verdicts.reason: The checkable parts hold. The workflows directory contains exactly test_qlib_from_pip.yml, test_qlib_from_source.yml and test_qlib_from_source_slow.yml. README lines 14-20 and line 48 route LLM-driven auto quant factory to RD-Agent. The releases API confirms v0.9.7 (2025-08-15) is still the newest, i.e. 13 months with no release while the default branch keeps moving (pushed_at 2026-09-22). The leading clause 'most complete organisation-backed platform' is an unfalsifiable superlative with no primary source and carries no evidentiary weight; nothing else is refutable. Unflattering context the claim omits: 480 open issues.

verdicts.claim: Reports ~2x higher annualised return than benchmark factor libraries using over 70% fewer factors at under $10 per run on real-market backtests; author-reported and not independently replicated.
verdicts.reason: Verbatim in arXiv 2505.15155v2: 'at a cost under $10, R&D-Agent(Q) achieves approximately 2x higher ARR than benchmark factor libraries while using over 70% fewer factors'. NeurIPS 2025 acceptance independently confirmed by the NeurIPS virtual poster page (poster/121804). Four targeted searches for a replication returned only the authors' own paper, the Microsoft Research page, the RD-Agent docs and secondary blog/YouTube restatements - no third-party replication, so the claim's own hedge is correct.

verdicts.claim: Only repository in the shortlist whose reproducibility has been independently measured and published by third parties, in a peer-reviewed study varying temperature, seed, top_k and top_p across GPT-4o and Qwen3:30B.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed: 'Reproducibility in the TradingAgents Framework', Polyachenko & State (University of Luxembourg - third party, not Tauric), IC-AIF '26: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Fintech, pages 365-370, published 2026-04-30. Abstract: 'We evaluate the TradingAgents framework ... using GPT-4o and Qwen3:30B models with varying temperature, seed, and sampling parameters.' (top_k/top_p are covered by 'sampling parameters' rather than named). IMPORTANT COUNTER-EVIDENCE the claim omits and which cuts against TradingAgents' merit: the same abstract reports both configurations UNDERPERFORMING the benchmark - Qwen3:30B 18.1% +/- 2.8% and GPT-4o 15.8% +/- 4.2% cumulative, versus 19.1% for Google buy-and-hold - on a single stock over three months (May-July 2025). A 6-page result on one ticker is a weak reproducibility base and its headline finding is negative.

verdicts.claim: ML4T's tests/ tree contains named regression tests for leakage detection, point-in-time GARCH features, purged/embargoed conformal coverage, CSCV, holdout second-look refusal and survivorship (ranking a bankrupt member last).
verdicts.reason: Every enumerated test exists in the cited tree: tests/test_leakage_detectors.py, tests/test_sp500_options_garch_pit.py, tests/test_conformal_embargo_coverage.py (plus test_conformal_coverage.py and test_conformal_calibration.py), tests/test_uncertainty_cscv.py, tests/test_holdout_second_look_refusal.py, and - the component I expected to fail - tests/test_candidate_set_ranks_a_bankrupt_member_last.py and tests/test_ranking_a_bankrupt_member.py. They run in the required `test-unit` CI job. The trailing superlative 'strongest open-source reference for research validity' is unfalsifiable and carries no evidentiary weight, but no enumerated fact is wrong.

verdicts.claim: The v3.1.0-artifacts release is the most reproducible published strategy-research corpus in the shortlist: 860 training runs, 1,119 prediction sets and 11,099 backtests across nine case studies, each bundle recording its source commit, with the release text disclosing one dirty-worktree build.
verdicts.reason: The figures are misattributed to the release. The cited release page's own contents table sums to 142 training runs, 163 prediction sets and 248 backtests across the nine bundles - not 860 / 1,119 / 11,099 - and the release text states explicitly: 'The full backtest sweeps are also not included, roughly 40 GB of run logs across the case studies.' The 860 / 1,119 / 11,099 triple comes from a different file, docs/what-this-is.md line 45 ('| All nine case studies | 860 | 1,119 | 11,099 |'), which reports repo-wide registry totals, not what the release ships. Only the SQLite registry.db metric rows cover the larger counts; the shipped predictions/models/backtest artifacts are ~7x and ~45x smaller. The provenance sub-claims ARE correct: per-bundle .release/SOURCE_COMMIT (83d7a9da / 73f066b4 / 64677fbc) and the disclosure that 'The sp500_equity_option_analytics build ran from a checkout with uncommitted changes'.

verdicts.claim: Qlib has a shipped point-in-time database (PR #343, 2022-03-10) and the only 25+ model benchmark table with mean and std over 20 random seeds, but every published number is CSI300 / China A-shares so US-equities alpha quality is unmeasured in-repo.
verdicts.reason: PR #343 'Support Point-in-time Data Operation' confirmed merged_at 2022-03-10T06:27:52Z (opened 2021-03-16). examples/benchmarks/README.md line 9 states verbatim: 'running on Qlib's Alpha360 and Alpha158 dataset with China's A shared-stock & CSI300 data respectively. The values of each metric are the mean and std calculated based on 20 runs with different random seeds.' The only result sections are '## Results on CSI300' and '## Results on CSI500' (the latter marked incomplete), with no US/NASDAQ/S&P section anywhere in the file - so the China-only limitation is confirmed from the primary source and is the strongest US-equities disqualifier in this shortlist.

verdicts.claim: RD-Agent(Q) is the only automated factor-and-model research agent in the shortlist with a peer-reviewed quantitative result (NeurIPS 2025), ~2x ARR with >70% fewer factors at under $10 per run - a claim with no public third-party replication and no US-market counterpart as of 2026-09-21.
verdicts.reason: Refuted on the final clause. arXiv 2505.15155v2 contains a section 'Empirical Scope and Generalizability' stating: 'To address concerns about scope, recency, and data leakage, we extended evaluation to another major Chinese market (CSI 500) and the U.S. market (NASDAQ 100). We adopted new dataset splits (Train: 2008-2021, Validation: 2022-2023, Test: 2024-2025), ensuring that both LLM backends have cutoffs completely or nearly prior to the test window.' A NASDAQ 100 evaluation with leakage-aware splits is exactly the US-market counterpart the claim asserts does not exist. This matters for the sub-layer's US-equities fit: the judge under-credited RD-Agent's US coverage while over-crediting qlib's, whose benchmark table remains China-only. The headline numbers and the 'no third-party replication' hedge remain correct.

verdicts.claim: TradingAgents v0.5.0 is the most thoroughly de-leaked LLM multi-agent trading framework available, withholding present-day vendor company profiles on a single shared rule so a vendor switch cannot reintroduce the leak, serving SEC EDGAR fundamentals as filed; its README says backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure, and it adds no transaction-cost or survivorship model.
verdicts.reason: Refuted on the leading superlative and the mechanism detail; the rest checks out. (a) 'Most thoroughly de-leaked LLM multi-agent trading framework available' is an unbounded comparison against every such framework and no primary source establishes it - the cited CHANGELOG cannot. (b) 'On a single shared rule' is not what the CHANGELOG says; the v0.5.0 entry reads 'A historical run is not served a present-day company profile by either fundamentals vendor. (#1300)' - per-vendor coverage, with no statement of a single shared enforcement point. Confirmed sub-claims: v0.5.0 dated 2026-09-18 with 'SEC EDGAR serves US company statements as they stood on the run's date'; README line 363 verbatim 'Backtest results are not guaranteed to match any published figure ... Treat the framework as a research scaffold for studying multi-agent analysis, not as a strategy with a fixed, replicable return'; and a recursive tree scan for cost/commission/slippage/surviv paths returns zero matches, so the no-cost-model observation holds. Independent corroboration of the weakness: the IC-AIF '26 study measured both model configurations underperforming GOOG buy-and-hold.

survivors: ML4T implements CPCV / deflated Sharpe / walk-forward / embargo as named tests with 61/56/68 code hits vs 0/0/0 in qlib and RD-Agent, executed by the required `test-unit` pytest job with a green run on main 2026-09-21 (caveat: qlib implements walk-forward retraining under the name RollingGen, 8 hits, so the 0-column is vocabulary rather than total absence)

Vibe-Trading has 690 Python test files (vs 415 ML4T, 72 TradingAgents, 37 qlib, 31 RD-Agent) with hash-locked dependency verification across ubuntu-24.04 / macos-15 / windows-2025 and a 3.11/3.14 pytest --cov matrix, green on main 2026-09-21T18:25:45Z

Qlib's CI separately tests the published PyPI wheel (test_qlib_from_pip.yml) and the source tree (test_qlib_from_source.yml plus a slow variant); its README routes LLM factor generation to RD-Agent; no release since v0.9.7 on 2025-08-15 (13 months)
RD-Agent(Q) reports ~2x ARR with >70% fewer factors at under $10/run in arXiv 2505.15155v2 (NeurIPS 2025, poster 121804); author-reported, with no third-party replication found across four searches

TradingAgents' reproducibility was independently measured by Polyachenko & State (University of Luxembourg) in IC-AIF '26 proceedings pp. 365-370, published 2026-04-30, varying temperature, seed and sampling parameters across GPT-4o and Qwen3:30B

ML4T's tests/ tree contains every enumerated validation regression test, including tests/test_candidate_set_ranks_a_bankrupt_member_last.py, test_leakage_detectors.py, test_uncertainty_cscv.py, test_conformal_embargo_coverage.py, test_sp500_options_garch_pit.py and test_holdout_second_look_refusal.py

better_alternatives_found.name: skfolio
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Both judges ranked five repos on 'strategy validation methods (CPCV, deflated Sharpe, walk-forward)' and concluded only a 1.2 GB book-companion repo implements them. skfolio is a scikit-learn-compatible, BSD-3 library that ships CombinatorialPurgedCV, WalkForward, MultipleRandomizedCV and optimal_folds_number as a stable public API (src/skfolio/model_selection/__init__.py exports them by name), with 214 test files, 2,427 stars and a disciplined release cadence - v1.3.0 on 2026-09-20, v1.2.9 on 2026-09-19, v1.2.8 on 2026-09-16. Against the ranked set it beats ML4T on reusability (a pip-installable library rather than notebooks plus a 6.8 GB artifact release), beats qlib on release discipline (qlib has shipped nothing since 2025-08-15), and beats all five on US-equity neutrality (no China-only benchmark constraint). Neither judge lens name-checked it.

better_alternatives_found.name: purgedcv (eslazarev/purged-cross-validation)
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: The most direct answer to the sub-layer's 'strategy validation methods (CPCV, deflated Sharpe, walk-forward)' component, absent from both rankings. README documents purged k-fold, embargo, walk-forward and CombinatorialPurgedCV with backtest-path reconstruction, plus deflated_sharpe_ratio, deflated_sharpe_ratio_full and probabilistic Sharpe, each mapped to its Lopez de Prado reference (D5.4, D7). All four splitters satisfy the sklearn splitter protocol and work inside cross_val_score / GridSearchCV / Pipeline. MIT, CI plus docs workflows, mypy-checked, distributed on both PyPI and conda-forge, has a CITATION.cff and a JOSS paper, mentioned in Awesome Quant, pushed 2026-09-04. Its weakness is adoption (35 stars, 2 open issues), which is why it should be compared rather than adopted blind - but on the named methodology it is a cleaner dependency than extracting utils/cv_splits.py out of a book repo.

better_alternatives_found.name: FinRL
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: The sub-layer explicitly names 'RL trading' as a SOTA strategy source, yet neither judge ranked a single RL-trading repository - the shortlist covered factor research (qlib, RD-Agent), ML pedagogy (ML4T) and LLM agents (TradingAgents, Vibe-Trading) only. FinRL is the org-backed reference implementation for that missing lane: 16,369 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-22, actively maintained by AI4Finance-Foundation, with a documented composable pipeline (stock selection, portfolio allocation, timing, risk overlays) and an explicit design goal of backtest/live consistency. This is a coverage gap rather than a claim refutation: the ranking cannot be called comprehensive for this sub-layer while the RL lane is unrepresented. Related org repos deserving the same treatment are FinRL-Meta (1,941 stars, pushed 2026-07-13) and TradeMaster-NTU/TradeMaster (3,080 stars but dormant since 2025-06-04).

judges.lens: Engineering quality for sub-layer T-data (US-equities market data, point-in-time datasets, data engineering): code/test/CI health, release discipline, API stability, documentation depth, dependency and platform hygiene, security/provenance, community and maintainer organisation, operational fit for Linux/WSL2 + Python 3.12+ + local-first. All judgments derive from public GitHub API metadata, primary repo files and public docs read on 2026-09-21; no file under <PROJECTS_ROOT> was opened and no prior project selection informed the scores. `quality_cost` is scored as engineering quality delivered per unit of operational/licensing/infrastructure cost, not as raw quality.

scores.notes: Columnar storage + validation is explicitly in this sub-layer's scope and DuckDB is the strongest local-first fit: in-process, single dependency, native Parquet/Arrow read and write. Engineering health is the best on the shortlist: top-level test/ tree, 42 Actions workflows including CIFuzz, Coverity Scan, sanitizer suppression files (.sanitizer-leak-suppressions.txt, .sanitizer-thread-suppressions.txt), Regression, ExtendedTests, NightlyTests, Client Tests and per-platform Linux/OSX/Windows/Android jobs. Release discipline is a clean semver train (v1.5.2 2026-04-13 -> v1.5.3 -> v1.5.4 -> v1.5.5 2026-07-22) with a maintained v1.4.x backport (v1.4.5 2026-06-17). MIT, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CITATION.cff, AI_POLICY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md all present; pushed within hours of the check. No equities domain knowledge is provided - it is substrate, not a market-data source.

scores.notes: Arrow is the columnar interchange substrate that every other candidate in this sub-layer depends on (Polars, DuckDB, Nautilus catalog, QuestDB via ADBC), and pyarrow is the practical Parquet writer for a point-in-time bar/tick catalog. Governance is the most formal on the shortlist: ASF project with .asf.yaml, and release discipline visibly follows the ASF RC-vote process (apache-arrow-25.0.0-rc1 -> apache-arrow-25.0.0 2026-07-10 -> apache-arrow-25.0.1-rc0/rc1 -> apache-arrow-25.0.1 2026-08-10). 43 workflows, a dedicated testing/ submodule, .pre-commit-config.yaml, clang-format/clang-tidy, hadolint and shellcheck configs. Apache-2.0, multi-language (cpp, python, r, ruby, matlab, c_glib). The format itself carries explicit stability guarantees, which is the strongest lifecycle-portability argument available here. quality_cost held at 2 only because the C++/Python build and wheel footprint is heavy relative to a pure-Python dependency; runtime cost is zero.

scores.notes: Under a T-data lens this is the strongest equities-aware data layer on the shortlist: ParquetDataCatalog is documented as a Python interface over a Rust catalog and a DataFusion query engine, with Arrow schemas defined in the model/persistence/serialization crates, plus a DatabentoDataLoader that converts Databento US cash-equity schemas (MBO -> OrderBookDelta and so on) into that catalog once for repeatable backtests. Supply-chain hygiene is the best observed anywhere in this set: .supply-chain/audits.toml + imports.lock (cargo-vet style), osv-scanner.toml, deny.toml, .gitleaks.toml, and workflows for codeql-analysis, security-audit and openssf-scorecard alongside build, test, nightly-tests, performance and docker-test. Process artefacts are unusually complete (ROADMAP.md, RELEASES.md, MIGRATION_V2.md, ADAPTERS.md, BENCHMARKING.md, SECURITY.md, CLA.md, AI_POLICY.md, 36-page docs/concepts tree). Deductions: LGPL-3.0 is a copyleft consideration for any redistributed derivative (fine for local self-hosted use, a real question otherwise), and the project is mid-major-version with v2.0.0rc5 shipping against a still-current v1.231.0 stable line, so API churn is active right now.

The input shortlist's has_tests=no is wrong: tests live at py-polars/tests and per-crate under crates/, not at repo root. 29 workflows, plus deny.toml (dependency licence/advisory gating), .typos.toml, dprint.json, rust-toolchain.toml pinning, SECURITY.md and AI_POLICY.md. scores.notes: Uniquely in this shortlist, Lean ships the hard T-data primitives in-tree: Data/equity/usa contains factor_files (split/dividend back-adjustment), map_files (ticker renames and delistings, i.e. the mechanism for survivorship-bias-free universes), universes, fundamental and tick/second/minute/hour/daily resolutions, and Data/market-hours/market-hours-database.json plus symbol-properties give exchange calendars and contract specs. Test engineering is serious: Tests/ includes RegressionTests.cs, ResearchRegressionTests.cs, a RegressionAlgorithms tree and TestData, with workflows for Build & Test Lean, Regression Tests, Research Regression Tests, Syntax Tests, Report Generator Tests, API Tests, Benchmarks and Python Virtual Environments. The deductions are all on the release and deployment axes rather than code health: the newest GitHub release and tag are both v2.4.0.1 from 2017-08-08 despite daily pushes, so there is no versioned artefact on GitHub to pin against; the code is Apache-2.0 but the complete US equity dataset is a commercial QuantConnect product (only sample data ships here); and the on-disk data format is Lean-specific, so exporting into an Arrow/Parquet catalog is custom work. C#/.NET primary with Python via pythonnet also adds runtime weight on a Linux/WSL2 workstation.

Engineering process is respectable (per-extension test workflows, CodeQL Advanced, pre-commit, ruff + pylint, .secrets.baseline, pytest.ini, conftest.py, openbb_platform/tests). The scores fall on three axes: AGPL-3.0 is strong copyleft with a network-use clause, which is a material constraint for anything hosted or derived and is the single biggest deployment risk in this sub-layer; release cadence has slowed (v4.6.0 2026-01-07, v4.7.0 2026-03-09, then only Open-Data-Platform tags in April 2026 and nothing since); and the poetry-managed multi-extension dependency tree is heavy.

scores.notes: Covers the 'validation' slice of this sub-layer, not market data itself - useful for asserting no-gaps / no-negative-prices / calendar-alignment invariants on an equities catalog. Engineering evidence is solid: tests/ tree, 18 workflows, a three-stage release pipeline (GE Releaser Tag -> Prep -> Publish), CODEOWNERS, CLA check and merge-queue CLA check, pre-commit.ci, .readthedocs.yml, lychee link checking, AGENTS.md, CITATION.cff, and Python 3.10-3.13 classifiers in setup.py. Cadence is steady (1.20.0 2026-08-07 through 1.23.1 2026-09-18). Apache-2.0. The provenance deduction is specific and verifiable: the repo now sits under the fivetran org, Fivetran announced on 2026-05-13 it would become steward of the GX open-source community and GX Core, and GX Cloud ceased to be publicly available from 2026-06-01 - so GX Core continues under new stewardship with no commercial product behind it. That is a governance change worth a dated re-check, not a disqualification. The 1.x line was also a breaking rewrite from 0.18, and the dependency footprint is large for what it does.

scores.notes: Provides universe metadata rather than market data: the README states 112,707 equities across 11 sectors, 80 industries, 117 countries and 84 exchanges, plus ETFs, funds, indices, currencies and money markets, and explicitly says the aim is NOT to provide up-to-date fundamentals or stock data. That makes it a current-snapshot symbol categorisation, which is exactly the shape that introduces survivorship bias if used as a historical universe. Test engineering is better than typical for a data repo: tests/ includes per-asset-class tests plus test_invariants.py and test_validate_identifiers.py, with .pre-commit-config.yaml and uv.lock. Licence and portability are ideal for local-first use: MIT, plain CSV/compressed files shipped in-repo, no API key, no network dependency, requires-python >=3.10,<3.16 with 3.12/3.13/3.14 classifiers. Release cadence is the weak point - 2.3.0 2025-04-04, 2.3.1 2025-07-05, then 2.4.0 2026-06-02 - and only 7 workflows.
