Provenance is unusually strong for research validity: this is the engine Quantopian ran a crowd-sourced fund on, and it is the reference implementation for Stefan Jansen's 'Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading'. Capability_fit is 2, not 3, because the portfolio-construction and risk-model half of the sub-layer is thin — zipline gives you an order/ledger/metrics substrate, not an optimizer or a risk model, so it complements rather than replaces skfolio/Riskfolio. Maintenance is the weak point and drives the 1: the five most recent commits as of this review are all dependabot action bumps (2025-11-13 and 2025-08-06), with the last substantive human change older still; single-maintainer, explicitly framed in the README as kept alive for book readers. Apache-2.0. Lifecycle 2: backtest-only in-repo — the Quantopian live-trading path did not survive, so paper/live parity requires an external bridge. Quality/cost 2: Cython extensions, bcolz/HDF5 bundles and a non-trivial ingestion burden.

unknowns: Whether the correctness defects in open issue #750 (CLA returning silently suboptimal portfolios; HRPOpt.optimize() broken on scipy >= 1.18) are fixed in v1.6.0 or still live — the issue is open, so the affected code paths are unsafe to rely on without independent verification.
Whether the Black-Litterman posterior-covariance concern in open issues #762/#763 changes results materially for US-equity universes.
No point-in-time, survivorship or corporate-action handling exists in-repo; correctness of inputs is entirely the caller's responsibility.
scores.notes: The only shortlist member in this sub-layer with a peer-reviewed software paper: JOSS 6(61):3066, doi 10.21105/joss.03066 (Martin 2021). Capability covers classical efficient frontier, Black-Litterman, HRP, Efficient CVaR/CDaR/semivariance, several covariance shrinkage estimators (Ledoit-Wolf with three targets, OAS, MCD), custom objectives, and — notably for US equities — DiscreteAllocation, which converts continuous weights into integer share counts given a cash amount, i.e. real position sizing rather than weights on paper. Transaction costs enter via add_objective/custom objectives rather than as a first-class turnover term, which is weaker than skfolio's formulation. Evidence 3: the JOSS review plus 20 test modules under tests/ including test_risk_models.py, test_black_litterman.py, test_efficient_cvar.py, test_discrete_allocation.py and test_readme_examples.py (which pins the documented examples). Maintenance 2 and not higher because of a real discontinuity: v1.4.1 shipped 2021-05-06 and the next release v1.6.0 only on 2026-02-26 under a new PyPortfolio organisation, so roughly five years passed with no release; the revival is genuine (python 3.14, pandas 3.0, dependency-footprint reduction) but its durability is not yet demonstrated. Documented failure modes are specific and open, most seriously #750 alleging CLA silently returns suboptimal portfolios on ordinary inputs — a silent-wrongness class that matters more than a crash for research validity. MIT, light dependencies, easiest adoption cost in the shortlist (quality_cost 3).

unknowns: US equities support: the repository's documentation set is futures-oriented (docs/list_of_futures_product_pages.md, docs/instruments.md, docs/data.md on futures data) and the README describes it as 'Systematic futures trading in python' — I found no in-repo equities instrument configuration or equities data pipeline.
Whether the GPL-3.0 obligations are acceptable for the intended deployment was not established and is a decision, not a fact.
Latest tagged release is 1.8.2 (2024-11-06) while master is pushed daily, so the supported install point versus HEAD divergence is unverified.
scores.notes: The strongest position-sizing and cost-accounting evidence in the shortlist, and the only candidate whose backtest and production system are the same codebase — which is the sub-layer's paper/live-parity criterion met structurally rather than claimed. Cost modelling is unusually principled: systems/accounts/pandl_calculators/ separates pandl_SR_cost.py (costs expressed in Sharpe-ratio units, Carver's method for cost-aware instrument and speed selection) from pandl_cash_costs.py and pandl_generic_costs.py, with systems/accounts/account_costs.py, sysproduction/reporting/data/costs.py and a live costs_report.py; spread costs are versioned data (data/futures/csvconfig/spreadcosts.csv) rather than a hard-coded constant. Volatility targeting and position sizing are explicit (sysquant/estimators/vol.py, systems/tests/test_position_sizing.py, systems/provided/attenuate_vol/ for vol attenuation). Evidence 3: the methods are documented in Rob Carver's published books and long-running blog, and the system has been run in production continuously since 2015. Maintenance 2: governance was deliberately hardened — Andy Geach took over as primary maintainer in 2024 and the project moved to the pst-group organisation in January 2026 with a stated two-owner rule for continuity — but the last tagged release is from 2024 and the README explicitly declines to offer support. License 1: GPL-3.0 is the most restrictive in the shortlist for downstream deployment. Capability_fit capped at 2 because the sub-layer asks for US equities and this is a futures system with an Interactive Brokers-only adapter; the sizing and cost methodology is portable, the code is not, without work.

unknowns: Point-in-time coverage for US equities: the PIT collector is CN-only in practice (scripts/data_collector/pit/ downloads quarterly CN data from baostock and the README itself warns 'the data might not be perfect'), so US point-in-time fundamentals must be sourced and dumped by the user.
Whether qlib's backtest exchange cost model (open_cost/close_cost/min_cost) has been validated against realised US-equity execution; no such study was found.
Whether the published qlib benchmark leaderboard results have been independently replicated on US data.
scores.notes: The only shortlist member that treats point-in-time correctness as a first-class, documented and tested subsystem for fundamentals: docs/advanced/PIT.rst states the data-leakage problem explicitly ('If we only use the latest version for historical backtesting, data leakage will happen') and describes a file-based PIT store keyed on (date of publication, period, value, _next); qlib/data/pit.py implements it and tests/test_pit.py exercises it. The backtest side is real — qlib/backtest/exchange.py, account.py, position.py, report.py and profit_attribution.py, with qlib/contrib/evaluate_portfolio.py for evaluation — and there is a dedicated tests/backtest/ tree. Evidence 3: Microsoft-authored papers and a maintained benchmark leaderboard, plus the in-repo test suite. Maintenance 3: pushed 2026-09-22, corporate backing, v0.9.7 tagged. MIT. Ranked below the top five for this sub-layer on two counts. First, capability skew: qlib's centre of gravity is signal research (alpha models, learning pipelines) with portfolio construction reduced largely to ranking strategies such as topk-dropout, so the risk-model and optimizer depth the sub-layer asks for is shallower than skfolio's or Riskfolio's. Second, market skew: the PIT machinery that is its distinguishing strength ships with a CN data path, and 480 open issues indicate a large unaddressed backlog. For a US-equities programme it is a strong reference design for point-in-time discipline and a heavy framework commitment otherwise.

unknowns: Whether the open correctness issues (#547, #546, #543, #537, #521, #516) affect the specific metrics a tearsheet consumer would rely on was not verified by running the code; they are maintainer-unanswered allegations with specific code-level claims, not confirmed defects.
Whether any downstream fork or wrapper has corrected the disputed formulas.
No benchmark or reference implementation comparison of quantstats metrics against an independent source (e.g. empyrical or a vendor tearsheet) was found.
scores.notes: Solves only the performance/tearsheet-evaluation slice of the sub-layer — three modules (stats, plots, reports) that turn a return series into metrics, plots and an HTML tearsheet, plus a Monte Carlo bust/goal simulation. It does no portfolio construction, no position sizing, no risk-model estimation and no transaction-cost modelling: costs must already be embedded in the return series it is handed, so it can neither detect nor correct a cost-free backtest. That is the core reason capability_fit is 2 and lifecycle is 2 rather than higher. Evidence is the weakest finding in this review and drives the 1: there is no paper, and the open issue list contains several specific, code-level correctness allegations against the metric formulas themselves — #547 claims conditional_value_at_risk mixes a parametric VaR threshold with an empirical tail mean and silently returns VaR when the tail is empty; #546 claims _prepare_returns silently converts missing observations to 0.0 returns in every statistic (a bias that flatters volatility and drawdown); #537 and #535 claim kelly_criterion is wrong by a factor of the average loss; #521 notes reports.html() assumes a constant risk-free rate; #516 reports inconsistencies among 3Y/5Y/10Y annualised returns. For a tool whose only job is to produce the numbers a decision is made on, silent formula error is the decisive failure mode. Maintenance 1: the newest commits are 2026-01-13 bugfixes for the 0.0.78/0.0.79 line and the issues above are open and unanswered. Apache-2.0, trivial to install; the cost is verification burden, not installation.

unknowns: Whether the Commons Clause permits the intended internal deployment: it bars providing to third parties, for a fee, a product or service whose value derives substantially from the software, which is a legal determination I cannot make.
Whether any portfolio-optimization capability exists in the open edition beyond the examples/PortfolioOptimization.ipynb notebook — the README places the feature in PRO.
No published validation of vectorbt's returns metrics against an independent implementation was found.
scores.notes: Disqualifying finding for this sub-layer, from the repository's own README: 'VectorBT is the open-source community edition of VectorBT PRO. PRO extends the library with parallelization, additional data integrations, portfolio optimization, pattern recognition, event projections, limit orders, leverage...'. Portfolio optimization — the first named requirement of T-portfolio-risk — is explicitly a paid-tier feature, as are limit orders and leverage, which also bound the realism of any cost or execution modelling done in the open edition. What the open edition does provide is vectorbt/portfolio/ (base.py, nb.py, orders.py, trades.py) for vectorised simulation and vectorbt/returns/metrics.py for performance statistics, tested by tests/test_portfolio.py and tests/test_returns.py. Maintenance is genuinely active (commits through 2026-09-17, a Rust engine, docs migrated to Zensical). License is the second problem: the repository badge reads 'Fair Code', and LICENSE.md layers a Commons Clause v1.0 condition on Apache 2.0 that removes the right to Sell, explicitly including hosting or support fees for a service whose value derives substantially from the software — this is source-available, not open source, and it is structured to steer commercial use to PRO. Evidence 2 reflects real tests but no paper or benchmark. Quality/cost 1: the open edition's capability is deliberately bounded by a commercial strategy, so its ceiling for this sub-layer is set by a vendor, not by engineering.

unknowns: Whether FinRL's own portfolio-allocation environments apply point-in-time universe construction or survivorship-free constituent lists — I found no such safeguard in the test or environment tree.
Whether the 312 open issues include unresolved correctness defects in the allocation environments specifically.
Whether any FinRL-published backtest result has been independently replicated by a third party.
scores.notes: Correction to the shortlist metadata: has_tests is recorded as 'no' but the repository does contain a unit_tests/ tree (unit_tests/test_core.py, unit_tests/environments/test_cash_penalty.py, unit_tests/agents/test_stablebaselines3_models.py, unit_tests/downloaders/test_alpaca_downloader.py and test_yahoo_downloader.py) plus .github/workflows/test.yml. Coverage is nonetheless thin relative to a 16k-star project and concentrated on agents and downloaders rather than on portfolio or risk correctness. On the lens, the evidence cuts against it and this is the one case where the strongest critique is published by the project's own research line: the FinRL-X paper (arXiv 2603.21330) states that offline backtesting environments of this family rely on 'oversimplified execution logic (instant fills at bar prices), unrealistic transaction cost modeling, absence of market impact simulation, lack of order book dynamics, survivorship bias, and data feed inconsistencies', producing 'inflated performance metrics' — i.e. the successor system is motivated by deficiencies in the predecessor's execution and cost realism. Independently, 'Unstable Gains: Multiplicity-Aware Evaluation of Financial Deep Reinforcement Learning' (Journal of Finance and Data Science / ScienceDirect S2405918826000309) argues that when trading policies come from non-convex stochastic optimization, a single reported Sharpe is not evidence without a multiplicity correction such as the Deflated Sharpe Ratio — which is exactly the evaluation discipline this sub-layer needs and which FinRL's headline results do not apply. MIT licensed and actively pushed (2026-09-22), but for portfolio construction, risk models and cost modelling it is a research testbed, not an instrument.

unknowns: Whether any maintained Python-side wrapper exposes QuantLib functionality in a form usable for equity portfolio construction — the SWIG bindings live in a separate repository not covered by this shortlist row.
Cost of building and maintaining the C++/SWIG toolchain in the target deployment was not established.
scores.notes: Exceptional engineering evidence, wrong layer. The README states the scope plainly: 'a comprehensive software framework for quantitative finance ... for modeling, trading, and risk management in real-life', which in practice means term structures, instrument pricing engines, stochastic models, calendars and day-count conventions. It has a large dedicated test-suite/ directory (initially missed by the shortlist's regex check and corrected there), CI across Linux/Windows/macOS/CMake, coverage reporting, a Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.1440997) and decades of continuous maintenance under a permissive BSD-style QuantLib licence — which is why evidence, maintenance and licence all score 3. But for T-portfolio-risk it offers no portfolio optimizer, no cross-sectional equity risk model, no position-sizing logic, no tearsheet and no equity transaction-cost model; date/calendar conventions and discounting are the only pieces that touch this sub-layer, and indirectly. Lifecycle 1 and quality_cost 1 reflect that adopting a C++ library with SWIG bindings imposes a large integration cost for capability the sub-layer does not get. Its legitimate role in a US-equities programme is derivatives valuation and fixed-income analytics, not portfolio construction.

unknowns: Whether the 'portfolio managers wishing to check prices or calculate risk measures' use case in the README extends to any cross-sectional equity portfolio risk model, or only to aggregating instrument-level derivative sensitivities — the source layout suggests the latter.
Whether GPL-3.0 obligations are compatible with the intended deployment.
No peer-reviewed paper or independent benchmark of FinancePy's pricing accuracy was located.
scores.notes: Same layer mismatch as QuantLib, with weaker evidence and a copyleft licence. The README self-describes as 'Valuation and risk models for a wide range of equity, FX, interest rate and credit derivatives' and lists its audiences as traders pricing or risk-managing a derivative, risk managers replicating price sensitivity, and portfolio managers checking prices — the equity content is equity derivatives (equity_american_option.py, equity_variance_swap.py, equity_vol_curve.py), not equity portfolios. Nothing in the sub-layer's requirement set — mean-variance or risk-parity construction, factor risk models, position sizing, tearsheets, equity commission/slippage models, point-in-time universe handling — is addressed. Maintenance is reasonable (pushed 2026-09-19, V1.1.2 tagged 2026-08-21) and tests plus CI exist, giving evidence 2, but there is no peer-reviewed validation comparable to QuantLib's track record. GPL-3.0 scores 2 for deployment fit: usable, but constraining for anything distributed. Included in this review only to record the mismatch explicitly rather than leave it implied by a low rank.

unknowns: Whether a portfolio extension exists outside openbb_platform/extensions/ (e.g. as a separately published package) — I enumerated the extensions directory and found none, but did not exhaustively search PyPI.
Whether Open Portfolio's APIs are available under any open licence, or only inside the commercial OpenBB Workspace.
Whether AGPL-3.0 obligations are acceptable for the intended deployment topology (the licence's network-use clause is the operative question for a hosted runtime).
scores.notes: Highest star count in the shortlist (73k) and, for this sub-layer, close to the lowest capability. I enumerated openbb_platform/extensions/ directly: commodity, crypto, currency, derivatives, devtools, econometrics, economy, equity, etf, famafrench, fixedincome, index, mcp_server, news, platform_api, quantitative, regulators, technical, tests — there is no portfolio extension. The portfolio-optimization functionality that older OpenBB material advertises is not part of the open-source Open Data Platform; the current portfolio offering, 'Open Portfolio', is described on OpenBB's own blog as an OpenBB Workspace App — a guest-authored commercial-ecosystem product covering position imputation, holdings evaluation and performance attribution — and Workspace is listed under 'Commercial' on openbb.co, not under Open Source. So a candidate selected for this sub-layer on OpenBB's popularity would be selected for a capability the open repository does not ship. What OpenBB does provide well is upstream of this sub-layer: data access, famafrench factors, econometrics and quantitative extensions. License_deployment_fit 1 reflects AGPL-3.0 (the shortlist verified this from the raw LICENSE text against a NOASSERTION API response), whose network-use clause is a genuine constraint for a hosted research runtime. Maintenance 3 is real and not in question.

sota_claims.claim: skfolio is the only shortlisted portfolio library that makes transaction costs, management fees and previous-weight turnover first-class terms inside the optimization objective while also shipping Lopez de Prado combinatorial purged cross-validation with purging and embargo, making it the strongest single answer to this sub-layer's cost-modelling and lookahead-safeguard requirements.

Riskfolio-Lib offers the broadest published convex risk-measure catalogue in open source (26 measures for mean-risk, 22 for risk parity), several of which — EVaR, EDaR and RLVaR — originate in its maintainer's own peer-reviewable research rather than being reimplementations, though its upstream regression evidence is a single test module with 7 tests.

zipline-reloaded remains the most thoroughly tested open-source US-equity point-in-time and transaction-cost substrate — dedicated slippage, commission and risk test modules plus a full tests/pipeline suite over split/dividend/merger adjustment machinery — but its five most recent commits are dependabot action bumps from 2025, so its safeguards are inherited, not actively developed.

pysystemtrade is the only shortlisted candidate whose backtest and production system are the same codebase and which accounts for costs in Sharpe-ratio units for instrument and trading-speed selection, giving it structural paper/live parity — but it is a futures system with an Interactive Brokers-only adapter and GPL-3.0 terms, not a US-equities tool.

vectorbt's open-source edition cannot serve this sub-layer by design: its own README places portfolio optimization, limit orders and leverage in the paid PRO tier, and its LICENSE.md layers a Commons Clause on Apache 2.0 that removes the right to sell hosting or support derived from it, making it source-available rather than open source.

limits: No code was executed and no library was installed or benchmarked. Every score rests on reading primary sources — READMEs, source files, test trees, release lists, open issues, licence texts and published papers — not on reproducing any result. Claims about correctness defects (quantstats #547/#546/#537, PyPortfolioOpt #750) are reported as documented, unresolved allegations with specific code-level content, not as verified defects.

Scores are per-repository judgments on a 0-3 ordinal scale under one lens; they are not averaged, summed or combined into any aggregate, and the six criteria are not commensurable with one another. The ranking is my ordering under this lens alone and would change under a deployment-readiness or execution-engine lens.

Several shortlisted repositories (QuantLib, FinancePy, OpenBB, FinRL, vectorbt) are scored low here because they address a different layer or restrict the needed capability, not because they are low quality. QuantLib in particular has evidence and maintenance at the top of the shortlist while being nearly irrelevant to equity portfolio construction.

Star counts and the shortlist's mechanical metadata were not used as merit signals and in two cases conflict with what I observed: FinRL is recorded as has_tests 'no' but has a unit_tests/ tree with CI, and OpenBB's 73k stars do not correspond to any portfolio capability in the open-source extension set.

Coverage is bounded by the supplied shortlist of twelve repositories. I did not run independent discovery, so genuinely state-of-the-art candidates for this sub-layer that were filtered out upstream (for example by the star-rank cut, the release-recency rule, or the licence rule) are invisible to this review; absence from this list is not evidence of absence in the field.

Evidence is dated to on-or-before 2026-09-21 and reflects repository state on that date. Release cadence for the most active candidates (skfolio shipped five releases in the week before this review) means maintenance scores decay quickly.

I could not establish, for any candidate, a validated survivorship-bias-free US-equity data path — the closest is Qlib's point-in-time store, whose collector is CN-only. Point-in-time correctness therefore remains an integrator responsibility across the entire shortlist, and no score here should be read as evidence that a tool supplies it.

Per the blindness rule I opened no files under <PROJECTS_ROOT> and used no prior project context; I did not check whether these conclusions agree or conflict with any selection this project has already made.

verdicts.claim: skfolio is the only shortlisted portfolio-construction library whose CI executes the full test suite on every push across Python 3.10 through 3.14 plus a minimum-dependency resolution job, with all of the five most recent runs green on 2026-09-21.
verdicts.reason: Every skfolio-specific fact checks out: ci.yml runs on push to main and PRs to main, the tests-linux matrix is 3.10/3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14 on 'latest' deps plus a 3.10 'min' job using `uv pip compile --resolution lowest-direct`, each running `pytest -q tests`, and the six most recent ci.yml runs (through 2026-09-21T12:20Z) are all conclusion=success. The EXCLUSIVITY is false. PyPortfolioOpt's .github/workflows/main.yml also runs on push to main and executes `uv run pytest ./tests` twice over a 3-OS x 5-Python matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows x 3.10-3.14) in `test-nosoftdeps` and `test-full`, i.e. a strictly broader OS matrix of the same suite. skfolio's genuine differentiator is narrower than stated: the lowest-direct minimum-dependency resolution job, plus the fact that it is actually green. The honest contrast is that PyPortfolioOpt's last push-event CI run on main (2026-07-07T21:13Z) ended in FAILURE and has not been fixed, and every PR run since 2026-08-24 sits at conclusion=action_required (approval-gated, never executed) — so PPO's matrix is real but currently unexercised and red, whereas skfolio's is real, exercised and green.

verdicts.claim: skfolio is the only repository in this sub-layer that pairs a scikit-learn-native optimizer/risk-model API with both an academic preprint (arXiv 2507.04176) and a citable Zenodo DOI, and it ships supply-chain artefacts (CodeQL, SBOM export, dependency review) that none of the other portfolio libraries provide.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed on every testable element. arXiv 2507.04176 resolves to 'skfolio: Portfolio Optimization in Python'. README.rst carries the Zenodo concept DOI badge 10.5281/zenodo.16148630 with both concept- and version-DOI citation guidance. The Actions workflow listing for skfolio shows CodeQL active (as GitHub default setup, path dynamic/github-code-scanning/codeql), .github/workflows/export-sbom.yml and .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml; the same listing for PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib, quantstats and zipline-reloaded shows none of the three (only Dependabot on each). ONE MATERIAL CAVEAT that does not refute the wording but undercuts its implied provenance ranking: the judge's own lens weighs 'DOI/peer review', and skfolio's arXiv 2507.04176 is a non-peer-reviewed preprint while a Zenodo DOI is auto-minted on release, not reviewed. PyPortfolioOpt has an actually peer-reviewed publication — Martin, R. A. (2021), Journal of Open Source Software 6(61), 3066, doi 10.21105/joss.03066 — so on peer review specifically PyPortfolioOpt, not skfolio, holds the stronger artefact.

verdicts.claim: Riskfolio-Lib offers the broadest catalogue of risk measures and allocation models among the shortlisted Python optimizers, yet no automated test runs on its pull requests: tests/ holds a single test module and the Test step in build.yml is commented out (lines 63-65), so its green 'build' jobs are wheel builds only.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed verbatim from the primary file. build.yml contains the commented block `#      - name: Test` / `#        run: |` / `#          source continuous_integration/test_script.sh` at exactly that position, immediately after the Install step; the `build` job therefore only installs dependencies before uploading a (never-generated) coverage artefact. tests/ contains one Python module, test_portfolio.py, plus nine CSV fixtures; that module defines 7 test functions. Two aggravating facts the claim omits: the build matrix is 3 OS x 5 Pythons yet still runs no tests, and every pull_request run in the recent Actions history (2026-09-16, 2026-09-17) has conclusion=action_required, i.e. approval-gated and never executed, so contributors get no automated signal at all. Breadth claim also confirmed: README lists 26 convex risk measures for mean-risk, 22 for risk parity, 37 for hierarchical clustering.

verdicts.claim: quantstats is the most widely adopted open-source tearsheet/performance-analytics package in this set (7.6k stars) but runs no tests in CI at all — its only test workflow, 'Test Pandas/Numpy Compatibility', is in state disabled_manually, which is precisely the breakage class its _compat.py and _numpy_compat.py shims exist to absorb.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed by the Actions workflows API: quantstats has exactly three workflows — 'Upload Python Package' (active), 'Test Pandas/Numpy Compatibility' at .github/workflows/test-compatibility.yml with state=disabled_manually, and Dependabot Updates (active). The eight most recent runs are all Dependabot dynamic updates; no test run appears. Star count is 7,651 (7.6k), the highest in the set, so the adoption claim holds. The shims exist as stated: quantstats/_compat.py (15,076 bytes) and quantstats/_numpy_compat.py (9,719 bytes) sit alongside stats.py (114 KB) and reports.py (89 KB). Aggravating: a tests/ directory exists in the repo, so the code is there and simply never run; and last push was 2026-07-20, two months stale relative to its daily Dependabot churn.

verdicts.claim: zipline-reloaded's scheduled CI has failed on Python 3.12 on ubuntu, macOS and Windows for at least five consecutive weekly runs to 2026-09-19 while 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13 pass, with no default-branch commits in 90 days to address it.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed and in fact understated. The ci_tests_full.yml run list shows EIGHT consecutive schedule-event failures on main: 2026-09-19, 09-12, 09-05, 08-29, 08-22, 08-15, 08-08 and 08-01. Job-level inspection of the newest run (id 35444314359) gives exactly the claimed pattern: 'Unit Tests for 3.12' failed on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-latest, while all 3.10, 3.11 and 3.13 jobs plus Lint Check and Formatting Check succeeded. The maintenance gap is far worse than '90 days': the newest commit on the default branch is 2025-11-13 ('Bump actions/download-artifact from 5 to 6'), roughly ten months before the collection date, and repo pushed_at is 2026-01-06.

verdicts.claim: skfolio is the only shortlisted portfolio library that makes transaction costs, management fees and previous-weight turnover first-class terms inside the optimization objective while also shipping Lopez de Prado combinatorial purged cross-validation with purging and embargo, making it the strongest single answer to this sub-layer's cost-modelling and lookahead-safeguard requirements.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed on both halves. _mean_risk.py documents and accepts `transaction_costs`, `management_fees` and `previous_weights` as constructor parameters entering the objective (with explicit guidance that daily-returns inputs require annualisation-consistent cost units, and a `fallback='previous_weights'` path). src/skfolio/model_selection/_combinatorial.py defines class CombinatorialPurgedCV with `purged_size` and `embargo_size` parameters, validated as non-negative, and documents that 'purging and embargoing can be performed' to avoid data leakage. PARTIAL OVERLAP worth recording: PyPortfolioOpt also exposes a first-class objective term `objective_functions.transaction_cost(w, w_prev, k=0.001)` returning `k * cp.norm(w - w_prev, 1)`, so transaction cost plus previous-weight turnover is NOT unique to skfolio; the exclusivity rests on management fees and on combinatorial purged CV, which PyPortfolioOpt, Riskfolio-Lib and quantstats all lack. The conjunction as written therefore survives, but the differentiator is narrower than the phrasing suggests.

verdicts.claim: Riskfolio-Lib offers the broadest published convex risk-measure catalogue in open source (26 measures for mean-risk, 22 for risk parity), several of which — EVaR, EDaR and RLVaR — originate in its maintainer's own peer-reviewable research rather than being reimplementations, though its upstream regression evidence is a single test module with 7 tests.
verdicts.reason: The counts and the test-evidence figure are confirmed (README: '26 convex risk measures' for mean risk, '22 convex risk measures' for risk parity; tests/test_portfolio.py defines exactly 7 test functions). The ORIGINATION claim is false for EVaR. Entropic Value-at-Risk was introduced by Amir Ahmadi-Javid in 'Entropic Value-at-Risk: A New Coherent Risk Measure', Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications 155(3):1105-1123 (2012), with 467+ citations — more than a decade before Riskfolio-Lib, and with no connection to its maintainer. Riskfolio's EVaR is therefore precisely a reimplementation of prior published work, which is the thing the claim asserts it is not. EDaR and RLVaR do trace to Cajas's own papers, so the claim is true for two of the three named measures and false for the one with the deepest external literature; as stated ('EVaR, EDaR and RLVaR originate in its maintainer's own ... research') it is refuted.

verdicts.claim: zipline-reloaded remains the most thoroughly tested open-source US-equity point-in-time and transaction-cost substrate — dedicated slippage, commission and risk test modules plus a full tests/pipeline suite over split/dividend/merger adjustment machinery — but its five most recent commits are dependabot action bumps from 2025, so its safeguards are inherited, not actively developed.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed on both halves. tests/finance contains test_slippage.py, test_commissions.py, test_risk.py, test_cancel_policy.py and test_transaction.py; tests/pipeline contains 29 modules including test_adjustment.py, test_adjusted_array.py, test_us_equity_pricing_loader.py, test_quarters_estimates.py, test_engine.py and test_international_markets.py, alongside top-level test_algorithm.py, test_blotter.py, test_ordering.py, test_execution_styles.py and test_data_portal.py. The six most recent commits are all Dependabot action bumps: four dated 2025-11-13 (download-artifact 5->6, upload-artifact 4->5, checkout 4->5, cibuildwheel 3.1.3->3.3.0) and two dated 2025-08-06. AGGRAVATING and worth carrying forward: because the scheduled suite has failed on Python 3.12 across all three OSes for eight consecutive weeks, those inherited safeguards are currently UNVERIFIED on the very Python version a 3.12+ local-first stack would target — 'inherited, not actively developed' understates the risk.

verdicts.claim: pysystemtrade is the only shortlisted candidate whose backtest and production system are the same codebase and which accounts for costs in Sharpe-ratio units for instrument and trading-speed selection, giving it structural paper/live parity — but it is a futures system with an Interactive Brokers-only adapter and GPL-3.0 terms, not a US-equities tool.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed on every element. systems/accounts/pandl_calculators contains pandl_SR_cost.py alongside pandl_cash_costs.py, pandl_generic_costs.py, pandl_calculation.py and pandl_using_fills.py, so SR-unit cost accounting is a named first-class module. The README opens 'Systematic futures trading in python' and states 'A fully automated system for futures trading (for interactive brokers)' and 'pysystemtrade uses the ib_async library to connect to interactive brokers' — futures scope and single-broker adapter confirmed, with no equities or alternative-broker adapter mentioned. License is GPL-3.0 per the GitHub API. The 'same codebase for backtest and production' exclusivity holds within this shortlist: zipline-reloaded is backtest-only, skfolio/Riskfolio-Lib/PyPortfolioOpt are optimizers with no execution layer, and quantstats is reporting-only. Note the repository has moved: robcarver17/pysystemtrade now redirects to pst-group/pysystemtrade (3,522 stars, pushed 2026-09-21).

verdicts.claim: vectorbt's open-source edition cannot serve this sub-layer by design: its own README places portfolio optimization, limit orders and leverage in the paid PRO tier, and its LICENSE.md layers a Commons Clause on Apache 2.0 that removes the right to sell hosting or support derived from it, making it source-available rather than open source.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed from both primary files. LICENSE.md opens with '"Commons Clause" License Condition v1.0', states 'the grant of rights under the License will not include ... the right to Sell the Software', and defines Sell to include 'fees for hosting or consulting/support services related to the Software'; the header reads 'License: Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause'. GitHub classifies the repository as NOASSERTION (spdx 'other'), i.e. not a recognised open-source license, corroborating 'source-available'. README line 55-57 states 'VectorBT is the open-source community edition of VectorBT PRO. PRO extends the library with parallelization, additional data integrations, portfolio optimization, pattern recognition, event projections, limit orders, leverage, and over 100 other features', and a later callout repeats that limit orders, leverage and contract multipliers are PRO-only. Since portfolio optimization is the defining function of this sub-layer, the open edition is excluded on capability as well as licence.

survivors: skfolio DOI/provenance/supply-chain claim: arXiv 2507.04176 + Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16148630 confirmed, and CodeQL + export-sbom.yml + dependency-review.yml are unique to skfolio across all four comparators (caveat: PyPortfolioOpt holds the only genuinely peer-reviewed artefact, JOSS doi 10.21105/joss.03066)

Riskfolio-Lib CI claim: Test step commented out at build.yml lines 63-65, tests/ holds one module (test_portfolio.py, 7 tests), build jobs install-only; PR runs additionally sit at action_required and never execute
quantstats CI claim: only test workflow (test-compatibility.yml) is state=disabled_manually, no test run in recent Actions history, 7,651 stars, _compat.py and _numpy_compat.py present

zipline-reloaded Python 3.12 CI failure claim: confirmed at job level on run 35444314359 (3.12 fails on ubuntu/macos/windows, 3.10/3.11/3.13 pass) and understated — eight consecutive weekly schedule failures, newest default-branch commit 2025-11-13

skfolio cost-modelling + CombinatorialPurgedCV claim: transaction_costs/management_fees/previous_weights confirmed in _mean_risk.py, purged_size/embargo_size confirmed in _combinatorial.py (caveat: PyPortfolioOpt also ships objective_functions.transaction_cost(w, w_prev, k), so only management fees and CPCV are exclusive)

zipline-reloaded test-depth + stagnation claim: tests/finance has test_slippage.py/test_commissions.py/test_risk.py, tests/pipeline has 29 adjustment and estimates modules, and the six newest commits are all 2025 Dependabot bumps
pysystemtrade claim: pandl_SR_cost.py confirms SR-unit cost accounting, README confirms futures scope and ib_async/Interactive-Brokers-only adapter, license GPL-3.0
vectorbt claim: Commons Clause over Apache 2.0 confirmed in LICENSE.md (GitHub spdx NOASSERTION), README lines 55-57 and 137-141 confirm portfolio optimization, limit orders and leverage are PRO-only

better_alternatives_found.name: cvxportfolio
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Neither judge ranked or even mentioned it, yet it is the canonical academic reference implementation for exactly the two functions this sub-layer weights hardest — transaction-cost modelling and multi-period position sizing. It is the Stanford CVX Research package accompanying Boyd, Busseti, Diamond et al., 'Multi-Period Trading via Convex Optimization', and it makes holding cost and transaction cost first-class composable objective terms (cvx.StocksTransactionCost, cvx.ReturnsForecast, cvx.RiskForecastError, cvx.MultiPeriodOptimization with a planning_horizon) together with a built-in StockMarketSimulator whose default cost parameters are documented as typical for the US stock market — i.e. the US-equities cost realism the shortlist otherwise only gets from the unmaintained zipline-reloaded. 1,290 stars. IMPORTANT DISQUALIFYING CAVEATS that a fair adoption record must carry and that likely justify keeping it below skfolio: every recent CI run of its single 'Lint, Test, Packaging' workflow is conclusion=failure (2026-04-27, 04-24, 04-23, 03-10, 03-09 x2), there has been no push since 2026-04-27, and it is GPL-3.0, which is a stronger copyleft obligation than skfolio's BSD-3-Clause or PyPortfolioOpt's MIT. It belongs in the candidate set as the transaction-cost/multi-period reference to compare against, not as an uncritical upgrade.

better_alternatives_found.name: ffn
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Both judges ranked quantstats last precisely because it runs no tests in CI, but neither named a maintained replacement for the performance/tearsheet-evaluation function, leaving that sub-layer function with no viable candidate. ffn fills it: MIT-licensed financial-function library for performance measurement and statistics, 2,678 stars, pushed 2026-09-20, with green CI on that date across separate 'Build Status', 'Regression and Version Tests' and 'Docs' workflows — including an explicitly named regression-and-version-compatibility suite, which is the exact breakage class quantstats papers over with its _compat.py/_numpy_compat.py shims and never tests. It is smaller in reporting surface than quantstats, so the trade is adoption breadth for actually-executed regression evidence.

better_alternatives_found.name: bt
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Unranked by both judges, yet it covers portfolio construction, rebalancing and position sizing with transaction-cost modelling as a flexible tree-of-algos backtesting framework built on ffn — the combination the shortlist otherwise splits between skfolio (optimization, no execution) and zipline-reloaded (execution, unmaintained). MIT-licensed (strictly more permissive than cvxportfolio's and pysystemtrade's GPL-3.0 and vectorbt's Commons Clause), 2,989 stars, pushed 2026-09-20 with all workflows green on that date, including a 'Regression and Version Tests' suite. Same maintainer as ffn, which is both an integration advantage (shared analytics layer) and a bus-factor concern worth recording against skfolio's organisation-backed maintenance.

judges.lens: Engineering quality for the Alpaca sub-layer (alpacahq org + third-party Alpaca adapters/integrations): code/test/CI health, release discipline, API stability, documentation depth, dependency and platform hygiene, security/provenance, community and maintainer organisation, and operational fit for Linux/WSL2 + Python 3.12+ local-first. Scored blind from public GitHub/web evidence dated to 2026-09-21; no project catalog, manifest or task record was opened. Capability_fit is scored as Alpaca capability specifically, not general engine quality, otherwise a repo with excellent engineering and zero Alpaca code outranks working Alpaca integrations. All scores are documentary: nothing was built, installed or executed.

scores.notes: Official Python SDK and the reference implementation for this sub-layer. Package splits into alpaca/{trading,broker,data,common} and ships py.typed; Sphinx docs tree (docs/api_reference, trading.rst, broker.rst, market_data.rst, migration.rst) and a docs build lint step gated in CI. Structured pytest suite under tests/{trading,broker,data,live,common} plus tools and a streaming-reconnect regression file; CI runs black --check then pytest. Apache-2.0, poetry-dynamic-versioning, 54 contributors, 55 commits in 90 days, v0.44.0 on 2026-08-11. Deductions: CI verifies only Python 3.10/3.11 on Linux, so the 3.12+ operational target is declared (python = ^3.10.0) but unverified; 87 open issues with the oldest still open from 2022-05-11, and stale.yml sets days-before-issue-stale: -1 so issues are never auto-closed, meaning the backlog is genuine rather than bot-pruned; release cadence is irregular (v0.43.2 2025-11-04 then nothing until v0.43.3 2026-04-24). NOTE: the supplied shortlist row claimed open_issues 0; the API reports 87.

scores.notes: Official MCP server; server.json declares 60+ tools generated from Alpaca's OpenAPI specs via FastMCP, with MCP-registry identity io.github.alpacahq/alpaca-mcp-server and a .well-known/mcp directory — real distribution provenance, not just a README. Best test design in the sub-layer for an agent-facing component: tests/ contains test_prompt_injection_envelope.py, test_trust_boundary_middleware.py, test_http_security.py, test_integrity.py, test_server_construction.py and test_paper_integration.py. CI is correctly split: a no-secrets/no-network core job on every PR, and a credentialed paper-trading integration job explicitly guarded by `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository` so fork PRs cannot reach secrets. Python 3.12 in CI, requires-python >=3.10, classifiers through 3.12, uv.lock, Dockerfile, MIT. Deductions: young repo (created 2025-06-03); fastmcp is pinned to an exact version (fastmcp==3.4.7), which is brittle for upgrades; 23 open issues (shortlist row said 0).

scores.notes: The most complete third-party Alpaca integration in this set, and the only non-org candidate with Alpaca wired through all three layers: lumibot/brokers/alpaca.py, lumibot/data_sources/alpaca_data.py, lumibot/backtesting/alpaca_backtesting.py, lumibot/tools/alpaca_helpers.py, plus docsrc/brokers.alpaca.rst. Of 22 Alpaca-matching paths, ~15 are tests (test_alpaca.py, test_alpaca_data.py, test_alpaca_oauth.py, test_alpaca_backtesting.py, test_alpaca_multileg_fix.py, test_alpaca_option_chain_quotes.py, test_alpaca_broker_smoke_apitest.py, test_smart_limit_live_matrix_alpaca.py and more). CI is substantial: lint + 6 sharded unit jobs + 4 sharded backtest jobs, plus agent-evals.yml, public-hygiene.yml, docs.yml, release.yml. 38 contributors, 100+ commits in 90 days, near-weekly releases (v4.5.86 through v4.5.91, Aug–Sep 2026), SECURITY.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md, company-backed. Deductions: GPL-3.0 is the decisive constraint — fine for private local operation, but it makes embedding lumibot in a redistributed non-GPL system a licensing event, unlike the Apache/MIT org SDKs. CI pins Python 3.10 throughout and ruff target-version is still py38, so the 3.12 claim is untested. Unit tests require ALPACA_TEST_API_KEY, POLYGON_API_KEY and THETADATA_* secrets, so fork contributors cannot reproduce the suite; full CI runs only on tags, main PRs or manual dispatch, not on every push. setup.py optionally bundles ThetaTerminal.jar, pulling a JVM into the build path. 90 open issues (shortlist row said 0); 91 patch releases in the 4.5 line implies thin per-release review.

Apache-2.0, 38 contributors, 33 commits in 90 days, and only 3 open issues — the only candidate whose issue tracker is actually drained. Deductions: single-version CI against a >=20 engines range is a real portability gap, and a Node/TypeScript SDK is not the runtime this lens prefers.

Two test projects (Alpaca.Markets.Tests, Alpaca.Markets.Extensions.Tests) with fine-grained per-endpoint files across trading, crypto, options, news and streaming clients; CI runs `dotnet dotcover test --dcXML=Configuration.xml`, i.e. it is the only sub-layer SDK measuring coverage in CI. scores.notes: DISQUALIFYING FINDING FOR THIS SUB-LAYER: NautilusTrader has no Alpaca integration at any tier as of 2026-09-21, so capability_fit is 0 on the Alpaca axis despite being the strongest engineering project in the set on every other axis. crates/adapters contains 19 adapters (architect_ax, betfair, binance, bitmex, blockchain, bybit, coinbase, databento, deribit, derive, dydx, hyperliquid, interactive_brokers, kraken, lighter, okx, polymarket, sandbox, tardis) and none is Alpaca; the ADAPTERS.md official table has no Alpaca row; the Community adapters table (document last updated 2026-08-24) lists only mt5-connector, sinopac-nt-community and tickerall-nt-community; a GitHub code search for 'alpaca' in the repository returns 0 files. RFC #3374 '[RFC] Alpaca Markets Integration' is still open (created 2026-01-01, last updated 2026-05-08, 8 comments), and PR #3375 'Alpaca adapter' (+11709/-1664, 50 files) was closed unmerged nine minutes after it was opened on 2026-01-01; a commenter on 2026-04-18 describes that PR as 'still in early stages -- not yet functional'. Everything else is genuinely strong and is why the other five scores are high: 12 CI workflows including test.yml, nightly-tests.yml, performance.yml, codeql-analysis.yml, security-audit.yml and a weekly openssf-scorecard.yml; deny.toml, osv-scanner.toml, .gitleaks.toml, .supply-chain/, BENCHMARKING.md; formal governance via CLA.md, ROADMAP.md, TRADEMARK.md, AI_POLICY.md and a written adapter tiering/demotion process; 100+ contributors and 100+ commits in 90 days; Rust core with pyo3 Python bindings, pinned rust-toolchain.toml, Docker. Deductions: LGPL-3.0 constrains adapter licensing (community listings must be LGPL-compatible); the project is mid-v2 migration (v2.0.0rc1–rc5 with MIGRATION_V2.md), so API churn is currently high; 129 open issues (shortlist row said 0); Rust builds are the heaviest compile cost in this set.

scores.notes: Solid, conservative Go SDK. 13 *_test.go files including rest_test.go, stream_test.go, trading_test.go and version_test.go (the shortlist's has_tests 'no' is wrong). CI is the best version-matrix in the org: go test -cover across Go 1.21 through 1.27, golangci-lint, a build step, and a `make generate && git diff --exit-code` gate that fails if generated easyjson code drifts. All GitHub Actions are SHA-pinned — the strongest supply-chain hygiene of the org SDKs. Apache-2.0, /v3 module path, static-binary deployment ideal for Linux/WSL2. Deductions: maintenance has slowed to 5 commits in 90 days, and releases are sparse (v3.9.0 2025-09-11, then v3.10.0 and v3.11.0 in May 2026); 43 open issues (shortlist row said 0). Known deferred toolchain debt is documented in the workflow itself: golangci-lint is pinned to v1.64.8 with the comment 'golangci-lint v1.64.8 supports up to Go 1.24; 1.25+ needs golangci-lint v2 + config migration', so linting lags the tested Go versions. testify is pinned at v1.7.0, which is old.

scores.notes: Genuine Alpaca automation with unusually good test portability. 32 test files including test_safety_guardrails.py, test_risk_position_sizing.py, test_bracket_protective_orders.py, test_chaos_resilience.py, test_backtest_engine.py, test_market_hours.py and test_import_no_network.py; CI runs pytest on Python 3.11 AND 3.12 with an explicit in-workflow policy: 'No API keys are configured on purpose: the suite must stay runnable offline' — the best offline-reproducibility story in this set, and the only candidate besides the MCP server verifying Python 3.12. Strong local-first fit: LOCAL_LLM_GUIDE.md, Ollama and OpenAI-compatible local endpoints, Dockerfile plus docker-compose.yml, ARCHITECTURE.md and QUICKSTART.md. Apache-2.0, 44 commits in 90 days, 17 contributors. Deductions: zero releases and zero tags ever, so it can only be consumed from a git ref; requirements.txt rather than a lockfile; effectively a single-maintainer project with no SECURITY.md or CONTRIBUTING.md; created 2025-07-03. It is an independent derivative of TauricResearch/TradingAgents (attribution is stated plainly in the README, and it is not a GitHub fork), which adds an unverified upstream-licence dependency. The README advertises a fast-moving LLM model catalogue, which is inherently high-churn surface. 1 open issue suggests the tracker is not a working queue. Architecturally it is an LLM-decision framework, not a deterministic execution engine — capability_fit 2 rather than 3.

Useful as a shell-level operations tool, not as a library or engine, so capability_fit is capped at 2.

scores.notes: The most disciplined small project here, undermined by its licence choice. ~25 files carry inline #[cfg(test)] tests (the shortlist's has_tests 'no' is wrong — Rust tests live inside src/). CI quality is high for a solo project: a build matrix over dev/release and no-default-features/all-features, plus a dedicated job that runs `cargo +nightly -Z minimal-versions update` and then builds against the declared MSRV 1.63.0, so the minimum-version claim is mechanically enforced rather than asserted. Published to crates.io and docs.rs with a maintained CHANGELOG.md, SPDX headers and rustfmt config; zero Python dependency makes it maximally portable. Deductions: GPL-3.0-or-later on a *library* crate is the most restrictive licence-to-role mismatch in this set — statically linking it into a trading binary makes the distributed work GPL, which is a materially different constraint from the Apache-2.0 org SDKs. Bus factor is 1 (Daniel Mueller as principal author, 16 contributors total, 10 commits in 90 days), and releases stalled for 19 months between v0.30.0 on 2024-12-29 and v0.31.0 on 2026-07-27, so new Alpaca API surface lags. 19 open issues (shortlist row said 0).

scores.notes: Agent documentation, not a runtime. skills/ contains just two areas — broker-api and trading-api (with backtest, paper-trading, paper-trading-cli, paper-trading-mcp) — so the capability surface is prompt assets that steer an agent toward the real SDKs. Governance boxes are ticked for a young official repo: CODEOWNERS, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, Apache-2.0, and a skill-check.yml workflow with SHA-pinned actions. But the only CI is `python3 scripts/validate_skills.py`, a structural/reference validator on PRs to main — no behavioural test exists, so evidence is 1. Created 2026-06-16, 3 contributors, 8 commits in 90 days, and no releases or tags at all, so there is no way to pin a version of the guidance; the shortlist row acknowledged the missing release object but let pushed_at satisfy freshness. Zero deployment cost and perfect portability (plain markdown, harness-agnostic) are the genuine strengths.

scores.notes: DISQUALIFYING FINDING: this repository is abandoned, and the shortlist's mechanical freshness rule was fooled by pushed_at. The default branch master has not advanced since 2022-01-02 (commit 475bb54); the pushed_at value of 2026-06-23 comes entirely from bot branches — the branch list is dominated by pyup-scheduled-update-2021-11-29 through pyup-scheduled-update-2024-12-09 and dependabot/pip/* refs. Last release v0.15.0 is dated 2022-01-02; 0 commits in the last 90 days. The shortlist row's justification, 'pushed_at within 12 months satisfies freshness directly', is therefore substantively false. It also targets a dead SDK generation: requirements pin alpaca-trade-api==1.4.3, and the upstream alpacahq/alpaca-trade-api-python is archived (1880 stars, last push 2024-12-02), superseded by alpaca-py. setup.py classifiers stop at Python 3.9. Testing is one file (tests/test_alpacabroker.py) and CI is CircleCI-only via .circleci/config.yml with no GitHub Actions. The README still tells users the sample strategies 'only work if you have a funded brokerage account or another means of accessing Polygon data', which reflects a long-superseded data arrangement. 57 open issues (shortlist row said 0). Apache-2.0 keeps license_deployment_fit at 2, but the exact-pinned dependency set makes co-installation with a modern stack impractical.

sota_claims.claim: alpaca-py is the reference Alpaca client and the only repository in the sub-layer that covers Trading, Broker and Market Data APIs in one officially maintained, type-annotated (py.typed) Python package with a published Sphinx API reference — but its CI verifies only Python 3.10 and 3.11, so 3.12+ support is declared rather than tested.

alpaca-mcp-server is the only candidate whose test suite explicitly targets LLM-agent attack surface — prompt-injection envelope, trust-boundary middleware and HTTP security tests — while splitting CI into a no-secrets core job that runs on every PR and a paper-trading integration job structurally blocked from fork PRs.

lumibot is the most complete open-source multi-broker Python runtime with a first-class Alpaca path, carrying broker, data-source and backtesting implementations for Alpaca plus roughly fifteen Alpaca-specific test files — at the cost of GPL-3.0 copyleft and a CI matrix pinned to Python 3.10.

NautilusTrader has no Alpaca integration at any tier as of 2026-09-21: none of its 19 in-core adapters is Alpaca, the ADAPTERS.md community table (last updated 2026-08-24) lists only MetaTrader 5 and SinoPac adapters, RFC #3374 has sat open since 2026-01-01, and PR #3375 'Alpaca adapter' was closed unmerged the same day it was filed.

alpaca-backtrader-api is abandoned despite passing a pushed_at freshness filter: its master branch has not advanced since 2022-01-02, its only recent refs are pyup and dependabot bot branches, and it still pins alpaca-trade-api==1.4.3 whose upstream repository is archived.

limits: The supplied shortlist metadata is unreliable and must not be reused as evidence. Every row reported open_issues: 0; the API reports 87 (alpaca-py), 129 (nautilus_trader), 90 (lumibot), 57 (alpaca-backtrader-api), 43 (alpaca-trade-api-go), 27 (csharp), 23 (mcp-server), 19 (apca). has_tests 'no' is wrong for alpaca-trade-api-go (13 *_test.go files), alpaca-trade-api-csharp (two full test projects) and d-e-s-o/apca (~25 files with inline #[cfg(test)]); conversely has_tests 'yes' for alpaca-backtrader-api means one file. Scores here were rebuilt from primary sources, not from those rows.

pushed_at is not a maintenance signal and the shortlist's freshness rule is defeated by it. alpaca-backtrader-api passed on pushed_at 2026-06-23 while its default branch has been frozen since 2022-01-02; the recent activity is pyup-scheduled-update-* and dependabot/* branches. Any mechanical filter keyed on pushed_at will keep admitting abandoned repositories — default-branch commit date is the correct field.

Relevance drift in candidate generation: the shortlist ranked nautilus_trader first for an Alpaca sub-layer on the basis of an open RFC issue, yet a code search for 'alpaca' across that repository returns zero files. Generic engineering excellence was allowed to substitute for sub-layer capability. This is precisely the synthesis bias the review was asked to detect, and it is why capability_fit was scored on Alpaca capability specifically.

Coverage of the sub-layer is incomplete in the shortlist. Enumerating the alpacahq org (77+ repositories) surfaces uninspected candidates: alpaca-java (official Java SDK, pushed 2026-09-21), agentic (plugin marketplace for Alpaca APIs, MIT, 2026-09-18), gamma-scalping (156 stars, MIT) and options-wheel (133 stars, Apache-2.0) as runnable strategy templates, alpacadecimal (65 stars), superpowers, and archived-but-informative alpaca-trade-api-python (1880 stars — the most-starred Alpaca repo, archived). Outside the org, QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca is actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-21) and is an engine-level Alpaca brokerage the shortlist omitted entirely while including an engine with no Alpaca support at all. These were not scored because scoring was constrained to the supplied shortlist.

Nothing was measured by execution. No repository was cloned, built, installed or run; no test suite was executed; no coverage figure was read; CI badge state and per-workflow pass/fail history were not queried. All twelve score sets are documentary judgements from README, workflow YAML, manifest, tests/ listings, release and issue metadata. Every Python 3.12+ claim in these notes derives from classifiers or setup-python config, never from an install or a run, and the license_deployment_fit scores reflect declared SPDX identifiers, not legal review.

judges.lens: Research validity and task fit for US equities: does the repository actually solve the Alpaca-integration sub-layer correctly (point-in-time correctness, look-ahead/survivorship safeguards, corporate-action and cost handling, paper/live parity, reproducibility), what published evidence, upstream tests or papers support it, and what failure modes are documented or observed. Scored only from public GitHub/web sources dated to 2026-09-21; no project-local catalogs, manifests or prior selections were opened.

I read file listings, README/SKILL/reference text, CI configuration, issue threads and release metadata. I did not clone, install, build or execute any repository, so no claim here rests on observed runtime behaviour, measured latency, actual fill realism, or reproduced backtest output. Every capability judgment is documentary.

The strongest available evidence is indirect: lumibot's in-code split-double-count rationale and its test names, and Alpaca's skill prose. Survivorship bias and delisted-universe handling is unestablished across the entire sub-layer. The Alpaca free-tier IEX feed carries roughly 2.5-3% of consolidated volume and free SIP excludes the most recent 15 minutes. This is a platform-level constraint that degrades research validity for every candidate here equally, so it does not differentiate the ranking, but it caps the achievable fidelity of any Alpaca-sourced backtest done without a paid data subscription and should be treated as a precondition rather than a per-repository finding.

A later comment (afrojuju1, 2026-05-08) describes another paper-tested fork, so private forks exist, but nothing has reached Official, Community or a listed External tier.

verdicts.claim: Alpaca's own backtest skill is the most explicit public statement of Alpaca-specific research-validity requirements: documented look-ahead bias for same-bar execution, an explicit --adjustment corporate-action mode, quoted-spread-plus-slippage fill formulas, benchmark parity on feed and adjustment, and a standing disclosure that paper results diverge from live.
verdicts.reason: Substance verified, with the cited file only half right. In skills/trading-api/backtest/reference.md: line 230 "**same_bar**: explicit request only; document look-ahead bias in notes.md"; line 131 documents `--adjustment` (default `raw`) and `--feed` (default `sip`); lines 212-215 give Buy fill = ask_price * (1 + slippage_bps/10000), Sell = bid_price * (1 - slippage_bps/10000) with the note that the bid-ask spread replaces the spread_bps assumption; line 362 "Benchmarks use the same execution assumptions, data feed, adjustment mode, and reporting cadence as the strategy" under "## Mandatory benchmarks" (line 347); line 350 forbids submitting live orders during a historical backtest. MIS-CITATION: the paper-vs-live disclosure is NOT in reference.md - it is in the sibling SKILL.md line 31: "Paper results may differ from live trading because of fill assumptions, market impact, liquidity, latency, data differences, order handling, fees, and other market conditions." Same skill directory, so the claim's content holds. "Most explicit public statement" is a superlative I can neither confirm nor falsify; the repo is Apache-2.0, 150 stars, created 2026-06-16, pushed 2026-09-08 - young, so its stability is unproven.

verdicts.claim: alpaca-backtrader-api is effectively abandoned for research use: it pins the ARCHIVED alpaca-trade-api==1.4.3, its last functional release is v0.15.0 from January 2022, its 2026 commits are dependency bots, and an open issue asks maintainers to add a deprecation warning for the archived dependency.
verdicts.reason: Every element verified, including the one I expected to fail. requirements/requirements.txt pins alpaca-trade-api==1.4.3; repos/alpacahq/alpaca-trade-api-python is archived=true. The releases list tops out at v0.15.0 published 2022-01-02T21:31:15Z. Open issue #1363 (created 2026-09-10) is titled "warn: Add DeprecationWarning for archived alpaca-trade-api dependency", and open issue #1128 (2024-04-23) is "backtrader-api uses deprecated alpaca-trade-api - will it be migrated to alpaca-py?" - so the deprecation-warning request is real and current. Minor precision point: there are no 2026 commits on master at all (newest is 2022-01-02); the 2026 activity is bot PRs/branches such as dependabot #1361 (2026-06-23), which is what the claim means and if anything understates the abandonment.

verdicts.claim: AlpacaTradingAgent's headline evidence is borrowed rather than its own - its homepage points at the upstream TradingAgents paper (arXiv 2412.20138) while its README calls itself an independent fork - and the LLM-agent backtest class it belongs to is documented to lose its entire edge once knowledge-cutoff leakage is controlled for.
verdicts.reason: Borrowed-evidence half fully verified; leakage half is supported but overstated. The repo's homepage field is literally https://arxiv.org/pdf/2412.20138 (the TauricResearch TradingAgents paper), while README.md says "An independent enhanced version built upon the original TradingAgents framework" and "an independent upgrade inspired by the original TradingAgents framework by Tauric Research" - and the GitHub fork flag is false, so it advertises a paper it did not author for a codebase it presents as its own line of work. It publishes no benchmark of its own; 271 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-09-05. OVERSTATEMENT: the leakage literature (Li et al., 9 Oct 2025 - FinLeak-Bench / FactFin, the arXiv 2510.07920 line of work, echoed by Look-Ahead-Bench arXiv 2601.13770) reports that Sharpe ratios of evaluated LLM agents fall by 50-71.85% past the knowledge window and that "most published LLM-based agents fail to beat baselines once their knowledge cutoff is passed" - a severe but measured decay, not literally the entire edge, and none of it was measured on AlpacaTradingAgent itself. The inference is class-level, so it is a prior about this repo, not a finding against it.

survivors: alpaca-py: CI matrix is exactly Python 3.10 and 3.11; 3.12+ support is declared via python = "^3.10.0" but never exercised. py.typed present; broker/, trading/, data/ all shipped; v0.44.0 on 2026-08-11 (source: .github/workflows/ci.yaml, pyproject.toml).

alpaca-mcp-server: tests explicitly cover prompt-injection envelope, trust-boundary middleware and HTTP security; CI splits a secretless core job from a paper-trading integration job structurally unreachable from fork PRs (source: .github/workflows/ci.yml).

lumibot: GPL-3.0 copyleft and every CI job pinned to Python 3.10; Alpaca implemented at broker, data-source and backtesting layers with 14 Alpaca-named test files (source: .github/workflows/cicd.yaml).

NautilusTrader (both lenses): zero Alpaca code in-repo, 19 non-Alpaca adapter crates, RFC #3374 open since 2026-01-01 with a maintainer 'not in the near term', PR #3375 closed unmerged in nine minutes and reported non-functional by a tester. Correction: the community table lists three adapters, not two - none Alpaca.

alpaca-backtrader-api (engineering lens): master frozen at 2022-01-02, refs are pyup/dependabot only, pins alpaca-trade-api==1.4.3 against an archived upstream; pushed_at 2026-06-23 is a bot artefact.

alpaca-backtrader-api (research lens): last functional release v0.15.0 (2022-01-02), 2026 activity is dependency bots, and open issue #1363 (2026-09-10) asks for a DeprecationWarning on the archived dependency.

alpaca-skills: the backtest skill does mandate documented look-ahead for same_bar, explicit --adjustment, quoted-spread-plus-slippage fill formulas, benchmark parity on feed and adjustment, and a standing paper-vs-live divergence disclosure - though that disclosure lives in SKILL.md, not the cited reference.md.

AlpacaTradingAgent: homepage advertises arXiv 2412.20138 (upstream TradingAgents) while the README positions the project as an independent upgrade, and it publishes no benchmark of its own; the leakage critique is class-level and measured at 50-71.85% Sharpe decay rather than a total loss of edge.

better_alternatives_found.name: OpenByteInc/QuantDinger
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Unranked by both judges yet the largest active Alpaca-integrating Python project found (11,956 stars, Apache-2.0, pushed 2026-09-21, created 2025-12-28). A code search returns 73 Alpaca hits including operationally serious files the ranked candidates lack: backend_api_python/app/services/live_trading/alpaca_activity_reconciliation.py (fill/activity reconciliation), alpaca_ownership.py, and a dedicated app/services/alpaca_trading/ client package. CI is split across basic-ci.yml, mcp-ci.yml, openapi-ci.yml and a dedicated security-ci.yml, which also undercuts the 'only candidate with LLM-agent attack-surface testing' framing around alpaca-mcp-server. Caveats: it is a multi-tenant SaaS / 'AI Trading OS' with billing and settlement rather than a local-first library, it is nine months old so release discipline and API stability are unproven, and its Alpaca layer is a service client rather than a strategy-lifecycle broker abstraction. Plausibly outranks alpaca-trade-api-js and alpaca-trade-api-csharp on Alpaca capability_fit for a Python local-first target.

better_alternatives_found.name: StrateQueue/StrateQueue
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Unranked by both judges. A Python backtest-to-live runtime with a first-class Alpaca path structured more granularly than several ranked repos: src/StrateQueue/brokers/Alpaca/alpaca_broker.py, src/StrateQueue/data/sources/alpaca.py, plus a dedicated tests/unit_tests/brokers/alpaca/ package (test_alpaca_broker.py, test_alpaca_broker_exec.py, test_alpaca_broker_orders.py, alpaca_stubs.py), a separate tests/unit_tests/data_path/test_alpaca_provider.py, a live integration test at tests/integration_tests/brokers/alpaca/test_alpaca_live.py, and examples/alpaca_order_smoke_test.py. That is a stub-based unit layer plus a segregated live layer - exactly the paper/live parity discipline the research-validity lens asks for. Caveats: AGPL-3.0 (more restrictive than lumibot's GPL-3.0 for hosted use), 214 stars, and last pushed 2026-05-19 - four months stale at the cutoff, so keep-but-compare rather than a replacement for lumibot.

better_alternatives_found.name: QuantConnect/Lean.Brokerages.Alpaca
better_alternatives_found.discovery_reason: Unranked by both judges. The official QuantConnect Lean brokerage plugin for Alpaca, actively maintained (pushed 2026-09-21T23:17:40Z, created 2024-06-07) and backed by both vendors - Alpaca published a joint integration announcement and QuantConnect documents it as a supported live-trading brokerage. It gives a production research/backtest/live engine a single-configuration Alpaca path with paper/live parity, the capability NautilusTrader demonstrably lacks and that alpaca-backtrader-api abandoned in 2022. Caveats keeping it off a Python local-first shortlist: it is C#, carries no SPDX license in the repo metadata, and has only 18 stars as a thin plugin repo (the engineering substance sits in Lean itself). Listed as the strongest engine-level Alpaca integration outside Python and a direct counterexample to treating 'no maintained engine ships Alpaca' as the state of the art.

Did not exhaustively page every query (per_page=20-30, single page each); deeper coverage of long-tail candidates (rank 25+) was not pursued given the primary finding below.

CRITICAL BIAS FINDING: naive `sort=stars` GitHub search in this environment returns heavily star-inflated/farmed repositories interleaved with legitimate ones. Verified examples: 'affaan-m/ECC' returned 264,775 stars (higher than anthropics/claude-code's 147,475), 'NousResearch/hermes-agent' 247,796, 'farion1231/cc-switch' 133,982, 'DietrichGebert/ponytail' 143,760 (a joke-description repo), 'nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill' 129,606 — all exceeding or rivaling canonical org repos like openai/codex (125,775) and google-gemini/gemini-cli (107,123) verified by direct `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>` lookup. This means star-count sorting alone is NOT a trustworthy SOTA signal in this dataset/time period and must not be used as the sole ranking criterion.

Mitigation applied in this run: cross-verified every promoted candidate against a direct `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>` lookup (bypassing search ranking) and/or required independent appearance across 2+ differently-worded queries before inclusion; candidates that appeared only once in star-sorted search with no independent corroboration (e.g. 'pi', 'herdr', 'Codewhale', 'ponytail', 'ECC', 'hermes-agent', 'cc-switch') were excluded pending manual repo-content inspection, since stars/pushed_at/description alone cannot distinguish a genuinely SOTA project from a farmed-star or name-squatting repo.

Coverage gap: did not run the required 'gh api orgs/<org>/repos' sweep for 3-6 organisations (time/turn budget spent on the star-inflation discovery and cross-verification instead); recommend a follow-up pass enumerating orgs/anthropics, orgs/openai, orgs/OpenHands, orgs/langchain-ai, orgs/block (or its successor), and orgs/SWE-agent repos directly.

Sub-layer scope only: this run covered F-agents (agentic coding foundation) per the computed task's blindness rule; it did not touch the trading/broker layer (e.g. alpacahq and beyond) mentioned in the relayed user request, which needs a separate discovery pass.

Did not independently re-verify every long-tail candidate's exact current star count via direct API call (only the promoted core set); several borderline candidates are flagged in their discovery_reason as needing that same direct-lookup verification before being trusted for the north-star manifest.

judges.lens: Engineering quality for the F-agents sub-layer (agentic coding foundation): code/test/CI health, release discipline, API stability, documentation depth, dependency and platform hygiene, security/provenance, community and maintainer organisation, and operational fit for Linux/WSL2 + Python 3.12+ + local-first. All judgments below come from public GitHub API metadata, repository git trees, primary README/docs files, release assets and public web sources dated up to 2026-09-21. No file under <PROJECTS_ROOT> was opened and no repository was installed or executed, so every score is documentary evidence, not measured runtime behaviour.

scores.notes: Deepest F-agents surface of the shortlist, verified from the git tree: OS sandboxing on three platforms (codex-rs/cli/src/debug_sandbox/seatbelt.rs, core/src/sandboxing/, core/src/config/windows_sandbox_config.rs, bundled bwrap release assets), first-party git-worktree isolation with integration tests (codex-rs/cli/tests/worktree.rs, core/src/worktree_trust_tests.rs, .worktreeinclude), subagent support with dedicated test suites (core/tests/suite/guardian_subagent_authorization.rs, mcp_subagent_elicitation.rs), skills and AGENTS.md instruction frameworks (docs/skills.md, docs/agents_md.md), an exec policy engine (docs/execpolicy.md), and BOTH Python and TypeScript SDKs (sdk/python with 10+ numbered async/sync example pairs, sdk/typescript, sdk/python-runtime). 1,249 test-matching paths of 9,345 total. Maintenance is the strongest measured: 9,855 commits in 52 weeks with the last 8 weeks at 211-393/week (the only shortlist entry still accelerating), 474+ contributors (GitHub caps enumeration at 500), SECURITY.md present. Provenance is the best observed: release assets carry sigstore bundles (bwrap-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.sigstore). Cost/quality caveats: 18,187 open issues is by far the largest backlog in the shortlist, the visible completed runs on main are dominated by bot workflows (CLA Assistant, Issue Labeler/Deduplicator/Translator) rather than a green test gate, repo size 638 MB, no dependabot.yml, and docs/sandbox.md plus docs/skills.md are one-line redirects to developers.openai.com rather than in-repo documentation.

scores.notes: A different layer from the coding clients and should be judged as such: herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer and agent runtime that 'owns their terminals' rather than wrapping them -- it runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode and others, marks each pane working/blocked/idle, survives SSH disconnect via a background server, and exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each other. That is a genuine orchestration/observability primitive for bounded parallel workers, and the tree confirms it: 10 worktree-matching, 60 skills-matching, 14 subagent-matching paths, an agent skill documented at herdr.dev/docs/agent-skill/. But there is no sandbox, no MCP and no SDK in the tree, so it complements rather than replaces a coding client. Best cost profile in the shortlist: 44 MB repo, one Rust binary, no Electron, 3,223 total paths. CI is the cleanest I could actually measure: the 'CI' workflow passed 12 of 14 completed runs on master with 1 failure, and a 'Distribution contract' workflow passed 8/8. Apache-2.0, dependabot.yml, nix flake, justfile. Deductions: only 99 test-matching paths; pre-1.0 (v0.9.1 plus rolling preview-* prereleases); 87 contributors; the README itself limits the persistence claim -- layout is restored after restart but 'the original processes do not survive'. Independently reviewed by third parties (Betterstack, June 2026), which is corroboration of existence and behaviour, not of engineering quality.

Excellent repository hygiene attached to a capability that does not match this sub-layer. Maintenance and release discipline are among the best measured: post-1.0 weekly semver releases (1.15.22, 1.15.21, 1.15.20), 1,185 commits over 52 weeks at a very even 18-36/week, 335 contributors, and a quality-gate workflow set that actually runs green on main -- 'Run Tests', 'Run Type Checks', 'Lint', 'CodeQL Advanced', 'Vulnerability Scan' (7/8 success), 'Code Quality: Push on main' (6/6). MIT, dependabot.yml, 1,165 test-matching paths, and an in-repo evaluation module (lib/crewai/src/crewai/experimental/evaluation/agent_evaluator.py). But for F-agents specifically it is a role-playing multi-agent orchestration framework, not a coding client, SDK, task queue or isolation layer: 0 worktree-matching paths, 0 queue-matching paths, and the 42 sandbox-matching and 324 skills-matching paths sit in a docs/templates tree rather than an execution isolation layer. Python hygiene note for this environment: requires-python = '>=3.10, <3.14', so 3.12/3.13 are supported and 3.14 is excluded. 449 open issues, but no SECURITY.md, and 33,153 of its 35,727 tree paths are under docs/, which makes tree-derived ratios misleading.

scores.notes: Explicitly retired by its own maintainers. The README carries a 'Maintenance Mode' badge linking to https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework and a CAUTION block stating 'AutoGen is now in maintenance mode. It will not receive new features or enhancements'. Metadata agrees: 0 commits in each of the last 8 weeks, 11 commits in 52 weeks, last push 2026-04-15, last release python-v0.7.5 on 2025-09-30, 1,089 open issues. Licence fit is the second problem and is a real hygiene defect rather than a detection artefact: GitHub resolves the repository licence to CC-BY-4.0 because LICENSE is the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 text, with the MIT terms in a separate LICENSE-CODE file -- a consumer must read both files to know what governs the code, which is exactly the ambiguity a foundation layer should not carry. Evidence is the one respectable axis: 376 test-matching paths and the AgBench harness (python/packages/agbench/benchmarks/GAIA and others) with a contrib-tests workflow. Capability fit for F-agents is weak regardless: a multi-agent conversation framework with no coding-client, worktree, sandbox or skills layer. Recommend treating as a historical baseline only.
